mainEntity.name: Do the drawstrings on your kids' swim trunks meet children's cord and drawstring safety rules for the EU and US, and can you make the waist without a free cord?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Our trunks and beach sets follow EN 14682, and we offer a covered flat elastic waistband, 2 to 3 cm wide, with no drawcord. Our tops follow ASTM F1816, so there are no drawstrings at the hood or neck. Waist drawcords are bar-tacked at the centre, with no toggles or knots. On under-7 sizes the drawcord stays inside the garment, and for ages 7 to 14 the free ends are 14 cm long at most.

mainEntity.name: How do you make sure white and pastel kids' swimsuits are not see-through when wet?

acceptedAnswer.text: To keep white and pastel suits opaque when wet, we use heavier fabric, a lining, a double layer or a lined front panel. During sampling, we check the suit wet and stretched, and that tells us which construction to use.

mainEntity.name: Can you print licensed cartoon or character artwork on kids' swimwear, and what licence authorisation do I need to provide?

acceptedAnswer.text: We print licensed characters, logos and trademarks only when you give us a written licence from the rights holder that covers the product type and sales territory. Send it to us before sampling. Without it, we can't sample or produce the artwork.

mainEntity.name: On front-zip kids' swimsuits, how do you stop the zip from pinching or rubbing the child's chin and skin?

acceptedAnswer.text: On children's one-pieces and rash guards, a fabric zip garage covers the puller under the chin, and a soft, full-length inner placket sits behind the zip. For toddlers, you can choose a 3-snap crotch or a front or back entry zip. Snaps have soft backing behind them, zips are guarded, and snap and puller attachments are tested to 90 N. For infants, the options are crotch or shoulder snaps and full-length front or back zips. Every zip has a soft guard running the full length of the track, so the teeth and metal stay off the skin.

mainEntity.name: Can you make separate fits for toddlers in swim nappies and for toilet-trained toddlers?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, we cut separate patterns. The swim-nappy fit adds 2 to 3 cm to the standard seat and rise and widens the leg openings, while the toilet-trained fit keeps the standard seat, rise and leg openings. We sample both for your approval before bulk, because a nappy layer added to a standard pattern changes the fit and the suit leaks or pulls.

mainEntity.name: Can you make tween and teen bikinis and tankinis with more coverage?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We make tankinis with more coverage, including cross-strap tops with swim shorts, as well as age-appropriate bikinis. Tops come high-neck or as sporty crops, and bottoms come full-coverage or mid-rise, or as swim shorts or skirted bottoms.

blocks.heading: Custom Baby Swimwear Sampling from Your Brief

We check stretch, hand feel, lining, trims and colours against your design and destination market. Once the design and size range are confirmed, we build and grade the patterns.
You get your [quote](/request-a-quote/) first, and we start sampling once you agree to the price.

A standard sample is ready in 10 to 15 days. Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against bulk orders.
We answer every [enquiry](/contact-us/) within one business day.

Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) confirms testing, documents, sampling and production schedules for the design and materials you choose, checked against your destination market and launch date.

items.heading: Your size run
paragraphs: We produce any baby, toddler or kids’ size run to your grading rules and size labels, and we set chest and waist measurements from your measurement sheet.

items.heading: Baby base chart
paragraphs: Our baby chart goes by height and weight: 0–3M is 55–62 cm and 4–6 kg; 3–6M is 62–68 cm and 6–8 kg; 6–12M is 68–76 cm and 8–10 kg; 12–18M is 76–82 cm and 10–11.5 kg; 18–24M is 82–88 cm and 11.5–13 kg.

items.heading: Toddler sizes
paragraphs: After 24 months, sizes move to our [2T to 4T toddler size chart](/children-s-swimwear-manufacturer/), set out by height and weight.

items.heading: Matching gift sets
paragraphs: You can pair a swimsuit with one or two matching hats, headbands or swim nappies. The print and size stay consistent, so the pieces make one coordinated gift.

items.heading: Gift set packing
paragraphs: We label every component for packing and restocking and pack it in your gift box, printed pouch or hanger card. Then we ship in 5-ply export cartons marked with the style, colour and size breakdown.

items.heading: Matching accessories
paragraphs: Our [custom bucket hats, scrunchies and headbands](/swimwear-accessories/) start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We make them in your swimwear fabric or print so they match the range.

items.heading: Infant openings and trims
paragraphs: Infant suits open with crotch or shoulder snaps or a full-length front or back zip with a soft guard, and carry no removable decorations. The pull tests and metal limits every trim meets are on our [children’s swimwear](/children-s-swimwear-manufacturer/) page.

blocks.heading: Sun-Protective Fabrics Made for Sensitive Skin
columns: What it means for your range
rows: For a range aimed at the pool, polyester keeps its colour and shape through repeated swims in chlorinated water.
For softness and beach use, nylon/spandex holds up to saltwater and sunscreen without losing quality. With frequent chlorine exposure, though, it loses colour and shape sooner.
We offer fabrics suited to sensitive skin, recycled and custom stretch options, UPF 50+ fabrics and quick-dry choices. We set print scale, lining and stretch recovery to match your design.

Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), we supply blends such as 80% nylon 20% spandex with matching linings, and we source LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE and Italian Carvico when you ask for them. For weekly toddler lessons, we specify the firmer [chlorine-resistant swim-school fabrics](/children-s-swimwear-manufacturer/) used in our children's range. Before sampling, we confirm that the baby fabrics, linings and trims you choose are certified to OEKO-TEX Standard 100 Product Class I for harmful substances, and the certificates go in your order documents. For the US, CPSIA calls for testing at a CPSC-accepted third-party lab, whose reports back the Children's Product Certificate (CPC) the importer issues; REACH is tested substance by substance. We arrange both at cost.

blocks.heading: Customisation, Decoration and Private Label Branding Options

items.heading: Style customisation
paragraphs: You choose the fabric, colour, print, size, trims, labels and packaging. We make solid or printed styles using cut-and-sew, digital printing, sublimation, embroidery and lining work.

items.heading: Comfortable decoration
paragraphs: On all-over polyester prints, the sublimation dye bonds into the fibre, so the print stretches without cracking. We keep embroidery and heavy logos away from areas that touch the skin, and we use flat printed labels so nothing rubs.

items.heading: Brand labels
paragraphs: Our [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels service](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/) adds your branding during manufacture. That covers heat-transfer care labels for tagless suits, recycled woven or printed labels, and logos printed after sewing.

items.heading: Printing inks
paragraphs: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-swimwear-printing/) prints your fabrics, digital prints included, with OEKO-TEX certified, environmentally responsible inks.

blocks.heading: Fabrics and Construction That Keep Baby Swimsuits in Shape
paragraphs: To stop the seat sagging when it's wet, we use 180 to 200 gsm nylon or polyester spandex fabric with at least 18% spandex. We add a full lining of 110 to 130 gsm at the seat. A suit gets heavier when it's wet, and stretch recovery and seat support are what hold its shape.

We use chlorine-resistant elastic at the waist and legs. Leg openings are finished with soft, flat elastic at gentle tension. Flatlocked or covered seams sit away from the inner thigh and crotch, so they don't rub while babies crawl and kick. For shape that lasts longer, LYCRA Xtra Life is available.

blocks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: How do you adjust infant patterns to accommodate a swim nappy without making the waist and leg openings loose?
items.answer: We add 2–3 cm of rise and seat room through the back and crotch. Soft elastic bindings, cut 10–15% shorter than the openings, keep the waist and legs close-fitting. Before grading, we check every infant fit sample over a swim nappy.

items.question: Can you build a swim nappy layer into baby swimsuits or trunks, or make reusable swim nappies to sell alongside them?
items.answer: Yes, we make both. Built-in layers use a soft inner brief with snug elasticated waist and leg cuffs. Separate reusable swim nappies come in sizes 0–3M to 24M and start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We settle built-in nappy features before the first fit sample.

items.question: For infant swim trunks, what waistband options can replace exposed drawstrings to avoid entanglement risks?
items.answer: You can choose soft elastic fully enclosed in a 3 cm fabric casing, a flat-front waistband with elastic at the back only, or a drawcord kept entirely inside the waist channel. Our kids’ trunks follow EN 14682, and under-7 sizes have no drawcords hanging outside the garment. We settle the enclosed-elastic construction before the first fit sample.

items.question: Do you make thermal-lined swim warmers as well as standard stretch swimwear?
items.answer: Yes. We make swim warmers with a soft brushed thermal lining for babies who get cold quickly, starting at 50 pieces per style in each colour. We confirm the thermal lining before the first fit sample.

items.question: Which baby-specific features, such as a nappy layer, zips, snaps, UPF fabric or matching accessories, add to the unit cost?
items.answer: Built-in nappy layers, guarded zips, snap closures, UPF 50+ fabric, all-over custom prints and matching hats or accessories all raise your unit cost above a plain lined suit, because each one adds materials and sewing time. Branded or recycled fabrics also cost more than our standard blends.

paragraphs: We're a modest swimwear manufacturer making [burkinis](/burkini-manufacturer/) and modest swim sets as two-piece or three-piece outfits. items.heading: Coordinated core range

items.heading: Headwear and cover-ups

paragraphs: Our ready-made designs are built on established patterns. That means your first order or market test skips new development and the sampling risk that comes with it. Once you have proven sellers, you can move on to custom development.

blocks.heading: Matching Prints Across Tunic, Leggings and Hijab

steps.heading: Enquiry response

steps.text: Bulk production starts once you approve the sample and pay the deposit. Your finished order passes inspection before it ships.

blocks.heading: Brands, Swim Schools and Teams We Supply
paragraphs: Where you sell decides what leads your brief: durability and uniformity, or fashion fit and regional coverage.

items.heading: Schools, clubs and teams
paragraphs: We supply swim schools, clubs, municipal pool programmes, and lifeguard and instructor uniform teams. For these buyers we focus on consistent, hard-wearing pieces you can reorder.

items.heading: Athletic and retail labels
paragraphs: We work with athletic modest swimwear brands and modest-fashion retailers in the Middle East, Southeast Asia and Europe. We adapt lengths, coverage and fit to what each region prefers.

items.heading: Market-specific size charts
paragraphs: We grade to EU, UK, US or Middle East size charts, or to your own chart, so your retail sizing matches your market.

blocks.heading: Coverage Levels, Sleeves and Swim Hijab Constructions
paragraphs: Choose coverage and headwear together. Tunic length, neckline and headwear work as a unit to control comfort and security. If you choose them separately, you end up with combinations that shift while the wearer swims.
rows: A mid-thigh tunic, a tunic with an added skirt or cape, or a knee-length swim dress with an overlapping or envelope hem. The swim dress is our longest style.
Pull-on full-neck, tie-back or adjustable, or a two-piece cap and drape. Sets can also take a hood or a separate cap.
Soft elastic binding keeps the face opening in shape without digging in, and extra room around the ears makes it more comfortable.
A long, coverstitched drape tucks inside the tunic. A shaped chin panel covers the chin and neck, and on adult styles an internal drawcord within easy reach adjusts the fit.
A lighter swim knit breathes better. The mill dyes it in the same dye lot as the tunic and leggings, and all three get approved together before bulk.
Full-length sleeves, with or without thumb-loop cuffs, or three-quarter sleeves. Necklines come as a small stand collar, a high round neck or a hood set into the shoulder seam.
Straight, tapered or flared legs, with an elastic or drawcord waistband.

blocks.heading: Fabric Matched to Pool or Open Water

items.heading: Standard fabric weight
paragraphs: Our 200–210 gsm fabric is rated UPF 50+. It absorbs little water and dries fast, so garments stay light when wet. Sport burkinis also get chlorine resistance.

items.heading: Pool or open water
paragraphs: Where your customers swim sets the specification. For pools we focus on chlorine resistance and colourfastness. For open water we focus on UPF and how the fabric behaves when soaked.

items.heading: Wet sample approval
paragraphs: Before you approve bulk, have your own swimmer try each sample wet, after washing, through full strokes, because dry swatches don't show cling or drag. The in-water tests we run on every prototype are set out on our [burkini](/burkini-manufacturer/) page.

items.heading: Lining and silhouette
paragraphs: Light shades need a front lining. Full or front-only tunic lining, a relaxed A-line with 4 to 6 cm of extra hip ease, and overlays at the chest and hips all reduce cling and hide the body's contours.

items.heading: Surface and shade
paragraphs: Matt or textured fabrics, a heavier 220 gsm tunic option, darker shades and all-over prints all show less of the body's outline when wet.

items.heading: Fabric sourcing choices
paragraphs: Our [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing service](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) supplies nylon/polyester-spandex fabrics with matching linings, including 80% nylon 20% spandex. On request it also supplies LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL recycled nylon, REPREVE recycled polyester and Italian Carvico.

items.heading: Standard UPF evidence
paragraphs: Our [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing service](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) provides documentation for UPF 50+ fabrics lab-tested to Australia/New Zealand's AS/NZS 4399. The rating applies to the fabric when it's dry and relaxed.

items.heading: Additional laboratory testing
paragraphs: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) you can order wet/stretched tests, tests on selected colourways, or testing to EU EN 13758-1 or US AATCC 183. You pay the accredited lab's fees at cost.

blocks.heading: Construction That Stays Put in the Water
paragraphs: To stop floating and ride-up, we don't depend on a single fix. We combine the cut, hems, inner layers and elastic finishes.

items.heading: Tunic float control
paragraphs: Elasticated or weighted hems, vents, a fitted inner layer and a close-cut waist keep the tunic from floating. Split or shaped hems stop it twisting around the legs during strokes.

items.heading: Legging security
paragraphs: Stirrups or cuffs keep leggings from riding up. Leggings sold separately get a wide, encased waistband that doesn't roll while they're worn.

items.heading: Elastic and adjustments
paragraphs: We control the elastic tension at the neck, cuffs and ankles and add silicone-backed elastic at the cuffs and ankles. Ties and drawcords stay within easy reach, and hoods are shaped to stay in place without pressing on the throat.

items.heading: Detachable garment parts
paragraphs: Detachable sleeves and skirts fasten with resin snaps or concealed zips, and each fastening is attached at a reinforced point.

items.heading: One-piece access
paragraphs: You can choose pull-on, full-length front zip, centre-back zip or half neck zip. Zipped styles have a fabric garage at the top and corrosion-resistant swim zips that work easily when wet.

items.heading: Built-in light support
paragraphs: For light shaping, we add a shelf bra with wire-free, removable contour cups inside your tunic or swim dress.

items.heading: Integrated lower lining
paragraphs: An inner brief or short in matching lining means the wearer doesn't need separate underlayers under the garment.

items.heading: Loose coverage cuts
paragraphs: Loose tunics skim the body instead of hugging it. Putting the volume through the shoulders, bust and hips instead of the hem controls drag and keeps full coverage.

blocks.heading: Size Ranges, Fit Blocks and Grading
paragraphs: Choose the classic or sport block based on how your customers swim. Your sales figures then show where petite, tall or curvy grading belongs.
rows: S to 3XL. The size M legging has a 76 cm inseam, and the tunic has 4–6 cm of ease at the bust and hip.
S to 4XL, an exception for sport burkini sets. The size M legging has a 76 cm inseam, and ease is 0–2 cm for a closer compression fit.
Both blocks grade by 1 cm per size.
Ages 3 to 12 in five sizes: 3–4, 5–6, 7–8, 9–10 and 11–12 years.
Adult hijabs come in S/M and L/XL. Children's hijabs follow the set's age sizes.
We adjust the legging inseam, tunic length, torso, hem sweep and slit position together, so the proportions match the regular lengths.
Our [custom plus-size collections](/plus-size-swimwear-manufacturer/) give you fully customisable styles, curvy fits and larger cup sizes.

items.question: How do your minimums work across a modest range of sets, separates, hijabs and cover-ups?
items.answer: Every style in the range starts at 50 pieces in each colour, from tunics and leggings to swim dresses, hijabs and cover-ups. Sold as separates, each piece counts on its own; how a complete set counts is on our [burkini](/burkini-manufacturer/) page. Decide on sets or separates before you order, because that choice sets your minimum quantities and how mixed sizes are packed.

items.question: Are your modest sets accepted at public pools that only allow swim-specific fabric and close-fitting garments?
items.answer: Our modest sets use swim-specific nylon or polyester-spandex, with close-fitting leggings and a fitted inner layer in the tunic. They meet the swim-garment rules at most public pools, but not at every pool. For pools with stricter rules, we offer close-fitting mid-thigh tunics and chlorine-resistant fabric such as LYCRA Xtra Life. The fabric composition goes on the label so pool staff can check it.

items.question: Can one retail set combine different tunic, legging and hijab sizes for customers whose measurements do not fit a single set size?
items.answer: Yes. We cut each component separately, so your retail set can mix tunic, legging and hijab sizes. We make these to order or pack them from separates. Each set is packed together, and every piece carries its own label.

items.question: Can you connect the tunic to the leggings to prevent separation in the water, and what attachment constructions can you offer?
items.answer: Yes. We join them at the inner waist with concealed ties, fabric loops or low-profile resin snaps. Before bulk production, you approve the attachment position, holding strength and comfort on the complete sample set.

items.question: Which hijab ties, hem weights and detachable fastenings do you modify or exclude from children's modest sets to reduce snagging and small-part risks?
items.answer: On children's sets, we use pull-on hijabs with no ties or drawcords at the neck or chin, we replace hem weights with elasticated hems, and we attach sleeves and skirts permanently. Every snap, ring, slider and trim is sewn or riveted on and passes a 90 N pull test.

blocks.heading: Burkini Sets and Matching Pieces Made in China
paragraphs: We make burkinis as two-piece or three-piece sets: a tunic and full-length leggings, paired with either a hood or a separate hijab. We make all the swimwear ourselves in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

To go with your sets, our matching [cover-ups](/cover-up-manufacturer/) include quick-dry swim skirts, swim dresses, long beach kaftans and robes in the same prints and colours. Full-length, long-sleeved options give the same coverage underneath.

blocks.heading: Fabrics That Stay Light, Opaque and Sun-Protective in Water

items.heading: Nylon-spandex drape
paragraphs: Our nylon-spandex drapes softly and sits closer to the body when wet, but it holds more water and dries more slowly. On premium lines, you can also choose a matte option with a softer hand.

items.heading: Polyester-spandex weight
paragraphs: Our polyester-spandex holds less water, so it feels lighter after a swim and dries faster. That makes it the right choice for full-length pieces worn all day.

items.heading: Full-length fabric comparison
paragraphs: You compare the two fabrics in full-length samples worn wet. Soaked tunics and leggings show differences in weight, cling and drying time that small dry swatches hide.

items.heading: Fabric sourcing service
paragraphs: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), we offer 80% nylon 20% spandex blends, matching linings and UPF 50+ options, and on request LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE and Carvico fabrics. They're lab-tested for chlorine resistance, colourfastness, stretch, recovery, strength, softness and durability.

items.heading: Sampling trade-off
paragraphs: Comparing both fabrics adds a development round and extra sample cost. For short sport cuts, the performance gap is smaller, so you get less out of that extra work.

items.heading: Wet opacity checks
paragraphs: We keep the garment opaque with a lining or a double layer, then check the finished piece both wet and under stretch.

items.heading: Recycled polyamide option
paragraphs: If you choose recycled polyamide, we offer fabric spun from reclaimed fishing nets and supply its certification with the fabric.

blocks.heading: Burkini Construction Tested in Motion

items.heading: Fastenings in motion
items.text: We keep only the fastenings your design needs. We confirm where each zip, tie and drawcord sits while the wearer moves the way she would in the water.

items.heading: Movement over standing
items.text: A standing fitting doesn't show whether fastenings stay comfortable during strokes or bending. Movement shows up rubbing, snagging and fastenings that shift out of reach.

items.heading: Fitting time trade-off
items.text: Fitting in motion takes longer. When it shows a pattern problem, another revision comes before approval.

items.heading: Seam placement
items.text: We run seams along muscle lines and keep them away from friction points, which cuts down contact in those areas.

items.heading: Bust support
items.text: We build in bust support with a compression shelf, and you can specify removable cups as an extra option.

items.heading: Protected, reachable closures
items.text: Every zip is chlorine-rated and has a full internal guard behind it. We place drawcords and internal ties where the swimmer can reach them.

items.heading: Coverage and matching pieces
items.text: Our [modest swimwear options](/modest-swimwear-manufacturer/) include three coverage levels, three hijab constructions (one is a two-piece cap and drape) and ready-made two-piece or three-piece designs with your branding.

blocks.heading: Lead Times and Seasonal Planning

steps.heading: Start the autumn before
steps.text: For a summer season, development starts the autumn before, because chlorine-resistant knits in specific colours get booked up early.

steps.heading: Book approved colours
steps.text: We confirm fabric and colours, then book the knit as soon as the colours are approved. Fabric procurement sets the schedule for chlorine-resistant swimwear, and committing to colours early leaves less room for late trend changes.

steps.heading: Finish fit details
steps.text: We finish the fit details while the fabric is on order. Through our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/), we check testing, documents, sampling and production schedules against your destination market and launch date.

steps.heading: Confirm order arrangements
steps.text: Under our [order terms](/faq/), courier delivery of a sample costs you USD 50 on top of the sample fee. We confirm your exact lead time with the order, and independent SGS or BV inspectors are welcome.

steps.heading: Run bulk production
steps.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive the deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season decide the exact time.

steps.heading: Inspect before shipment
steps.text: Our [quality checks](/about-us/) cover incoming fabric, cutting and sewing. After that come random checks and a full final inspection before shipment.

blocks.heading: OEM Burkini Design, Sampling and Water Testing

steps.heading: Develop your starting point
steps.text: Our [Development service](/development/) turns your design, picture or idea into OEM or ODM patterns and fit. We grade S to 3XL free of charge against US, EU or UK size charts.

steps.heading: Set the sample timing
steps.text: A standard sample takes us 10 to 15 days, so you have a physical garment to assess before bulk production.

steps.heading: Confirm development fees
steps.text: Each sample costs USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design, which covers its pattern or print in all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

steps.heading: Swim-test the prototype
steps.text: A fit model swims in every prototype while we check drag, shifting, cling and wet opacity. Once it's dry, we inspect it again to find any construction or fabric problems.

steps.heading: Test with your customers
steps.text: After our swim tests, you wear-test the revised prototype on your customers' body types and swimming movements, because fit and comfort depend on shape and use.

steps.heading: Approve after feedback
steps.text: We recommend approving the pre-production sample after your customers have wear-tested it.

items.heading: Support and pricing

items.heading: Order minimum

items.heading: First trial run

items.heading: Payment terms

items.heading: Shipping terms

blocks.heading: Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you manufacture burkinis using fabric we supply, and what stretch, recovery and wet-opacity requirements must it meet?
items.answer: Yes. We manufacture burkinis from your fabric if it has at least 50% stretch in both directions, at least 90% recovery and full opacity when wet and stretched. If it isn't opaque enough, it needs a lining, and lining changes the weight, feel and drying time. We accept fabric by testing a sample first. That adds testing time, and it settles whether you need lining before you supply the full minimum in each colour plus a cutting allowance.

items.question: Does a complete burkini set count as one piece towards the 50-piece MOQ, and can I order the hijab or leggings separately?
items.answer: Yes. A complete set of tunic, leggings and hood or hijab counts as one piece towards our minimum of 50 pieces per style in each colour. You can also order hijabs or leggings separately, and each separate piece has its own minimum of 50 pieces per colour.

items.question: Apart from tunic-and-leggings sets, can you also make one-piece full-body burkinis, sporty athletic burkinis, and swim dresses or skirts?
items.answer: Yes, we make all of these styles. Our one-piece full-body burkinis are close, streamlined suits that cover both the top and the legs. Sport burkinis pair a shorter fitted tunic with athletic leggings, and swim dresses and swim skirts are worn over leggings.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which fabrics do you offer that have UPF 50+ sun protection and resist chlorine and salt water?
items.answer: We offer UPF 50+ fabrics. On request, we also offer chlorine-resistant fabrics such as LYCRA Xtra Life. Our partner lab tests fabrics for chlorine resistance and colour fastness after repeated chlorine exposure. Our stretch and recovery testing checks that the suit returns to shape after wear and time in the water. We also test strength, softness and durability.

items.question: Can you grade our styles across an extended size range, including plus sizes and kids' sizes?
items.answer: Yes. We make styles for women, men and children, grading women's XS–3XL and men's S–3XL against US, EU or UK charts. We also produce fully customisable plus-size collections with curvy fits and larger cup sizes. Grading within these ranges is free, and we refine the fit as we build each size. You can send us your own size chart, measurement sheet or reference garment, and we cut to it. Once the chart is based on your fit model, we check every production piece against it and set grading rules separately for each style. If you don't have a chart yet, our pattern makers prepare one for your target market. We cover the EU, UK, US, Australia and the Middle East. We also prepare team size charts for club and school programmes. For a new fit, approve the base-size sample on your own fit model in the exact production fabric. That gives us the correct starting point before we fix the grading rules. Swim fabrics differ in stretch and recovery. If you change the fabric, the same pattern fits tighter or looser, and grading from a wrong base carries that error into every size. This approval adds a sampling round and lead time. For repeat styles in a fabric we've already fitted, it matters less.

items.question: Which ways can you put our logo and artwork on the garments: sublimation, screen print, heat transfer or embroidery?
items.answer: We apply logos and artwork with sublimation, screen printing, heat transfer or embroidery. We also offer silicone printing and silicone patches. Your branding also goes on sewn-in labels or woven waistbands, and we provide product-specific branding. For club programmes, we recommend sublimation. Labels and care notes get a partner's chlorine-resistant screen print. We also handle labelling and packaging. That includes branded hang tags, poly bags, retail packaging and printed cartons. For kids' swimwear, we provide branded size labels and packaging.

blocks.heading: Rash Guards for Women, Men, Swim Schools and Teams
paragraphs: We make rash guards in compression and relaxed cuts for surfing, swimming, watersports, swim camps and custom team ranges, and you can order collections for women, men, swim schools and clubs.

For women, we offer long sleeves for full UV coverage, short and cap sleeves, zip fronts, fitted or relaxed cuts, and plus sizes that are graded accurately. For men, there are long and short sleeves, compression shirts for training and relaxed styles for surfing, and we add custom branding for your team.

blocks.heading: Our Own Rash Guard Factory in Guangzhou, China

items.heading: Our own factory
paragraphs: We make rash guards and swimwear ourselves in one factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China, so your production is never passed to another manufacturer.

items.heading: Resort and hotel ranges
paragraphs: We also make custom-branded swim rash guards for resort and hotel programmes, with your branding applied across the collection.

items.heading: Factory ownership and checks
paragraphs: With our [factory ownership and quality controls](/about-us/), production and export sit within one company. We check at fabric arrival, cutting and sewing, then carry out random checks and a full final inspection.

items.heading: Enquiry response time
paragraphs: When you [contact our factory](/contact-us/), we reply to every enquiry within one business day, so you know when you'll hear from us.

blocks.heading: OEM Rash Guard Orders: Minimums, Samples, Lead Times and Payment
paragraphs: We quote factory-direct after reviewing your design and fabric, not from online prices. Under our [pricing and sample-delivery terms](/faq/), samples ship by courier for USD 50 extra.

items.heading: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which gives small and growing labels a starting quantity they can reach.

items.heading: First trial run
items.text: We agree your first trial quantity case by case. How flexible we can be depends on what production allows.

items.heading: Standard samples
items.text: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days and costs USD 50. We don't refund this fee or credit it against bulk.

items.heading: Design fees
items.text: Each design costs USD 50, which covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. We don't refund this fee or credit it against bulk.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

items.heading: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship FOB, CIF or DDP. With worldwide DDP, you get one all-in price delivered to your door, and we handle duties, customs and freight through our forwarding partners.

items.heading: Quote before sampling
items.text: Through our [quote process](/request-a-quote/), we price your order first and only start the sample once you agree to the price.

blocks.heading: Rash Guard Fabrics, UPF Ratings and Certifications
paragraphs: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), we source 80/20 nylon-spandex with matching linings, and we supply AS/NZS 4399 UPF 50+ documentation; extra lab testing is charged at cost.

items.heading: Performance fabric range
paragraphs: Our four-way-stretch, UV-protective polyester-spandex weighs 180gsm to 320gsm. Water temperature and activity decide the weight first. Board contact and sun exposure decide the fibre.

items.heading: Lightweight warm-water fabrics
paragraphs: At 180 to 200gsm, these fabrics hold little heat and air-dry in about 30 minutes. They suit warm-water surfing, swim lessons and long days in the sun.

items.heading: Heavier supportive fabrics
paragraphs: At 260 to 320gsm, these fabrics keep wearers warmer in cooler water and give firmer compression and muscle support for training and watersports. The trade-off is that they take about 60 minutes to dry.

items.heading: Repeated board contact
paragraphs: For repeated board contact, we recommend tightly knitted 200–240 GSM polyester-spandex or 80/20 nylon-spandex. Nylon stands up to rubbing best, and polyester holds its colour better in sun and salt water.

items.heading: Surface wear
paragraphs: For frequent surfing, we recommend fabrics of 190 GSM or more; mesh and brushed fabrics wear faster against boards and wax.

items.heading: Recycled fabric option
paragraphs: For eco-focused ranges, we offer on request a 190 g/m² fabric made of 78% recycled nylon and 22% spandex. It's rated UPF 50+ and holds GRS and OEKO-TEX certification.

items.heading: Training and surf protection
paragraphs: You can choose moisture-wicking, four-way-stretch, UV-protective blends. We use quick-drying, moisture-wicking fabric for training and UPF 50+ fabric for surf and watersports styles.

items.heading: Production certifications
paragraphs: Our [production certifications](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

blocks.heading: Sizes, Sleeve Options, Necklines and Fits You Can Order

items.heading: Size range
items.text: Our standard sizing runs from XS to 3XL, and we extend it up to 5XL for your plus-size ranges.

items.heading: Sleeves and necklines
items.text: Choose short, long or ¾ sleeves with a crew neck, high neck or quarter-zip neck.

items.heading: Compression fit
items.text: Compression fit stays in place and supports muscles during surfing and training. Because it fits tighter, it needs its own size chart or a wear-test.

items.heading: Regular fit
items.text: Regular fit puts comfort first for children, swim lessons and resort wear. Back-zip styles make it easier for kids to get dressed and undressed.

items.heading: Coverage details
items.text: High necks and cuff thumb loops cover the neck and arms for surfers and swim-school coaches, and the loops keep long sleeves in place.

items.heading: Hooded styles
items.text: We make hooded rash guards for extra sun cover in surf and family ranges.

blocks.heading: Flatlock and Bonded Seams Built for Board and Water
paragraphs: Every seam gets durable flatlock stitching by default. It works with every fabric we use and comes on every order at standard cost. On compression-fit styles, we place the seams ergonomically.

On orders of 300 pieces or more, you can choose bonded body seams for a cleaner, flatter finish, at a higher cost. Bonding needs a smooth polyester-spandex or nylon-spandex knit at 180–240 GSM. Mesh, brushed thermal, textured fabrics and anything over 240 GSM don't qualify, because the tape can't grip them evenly.
Even on bonded styles, we keep flatlock stitching at the high-stress joins: zip openings, thumb loops, hood joins and underarm gussets.

visuals.caption: Flatlock and bonded seams compared.

blocks.heading: Custom Rash Guard Printing, Logos and Names

items.heading: Full sublimation printing
paragraphs: For multi-colour, detailed all-over designs, we print edge to edge in unlimited colours. Sublimation dyes the polyester fibres, so the print doesn't crack or peel and the fabric keeps its stretch.

items.heading: Simple logo methods
paragraphs: Screen printing suits designs with up to three colours. Screen printing or heat transfer puts simple logos onto pre-dyed fabric efficiently, and we help you choose the method.

items.heading: Brand colour matching
paragraphs: We match sublimated rash guards to your exact brand colours and specifications, and we explain the dark-shade limitation before you approve the design.

items.heading: Dark shade limitation
paragraphs: Sublimated black and very dark shades look less deep than fabric dyed in those colours before printing, and that difference stays in the finished garment.

items.heading: Individual team personalisation
paragraphs: We personalise each piece with its own name or number, and we offer full sublimation for your custom team rash guards.

blocks.heading: Private Label Rash Guards and Design Customisation

items.heading: Private label services
items.text: With our OEM and private label services, you customise the colours, prints, logos, branding and fabric, and add private labels and custom packaging.

items.heading: Design starting points
items.text: Our [OEM and ODM development](/development/) starts from your design, picture or idea. Our team either creates the garment or works from your artwork.

items.heading: Panels and stitching
items.text: We offer colour-blocked or contrast body panels and contrast flatlock thread. Fix these choices, and any mesh inserts, in your spec sheet before sampling.

items.heading: Breathable mesh inserts
items.text: Mesh at the underarms, sides or back makes the garment more breathable but reduces sun coverage in those areas. That makes it right for training and warm-water styles rather than sun-protection ranges.

items.heading: Changes after sampling
items.text: Changing panels or inserts alters the pattern, print layout and fabric use, so any change after sampling needs a new sample.

blocks.heading: OEM Rash Guards with Your Own Fabric and Trims
paragraphs: If you supply branded trims, our [Swimwear Hardware](/swimwear-hardware/) team checks 2 test pieces of each; send the bulk quantity plus 3% extra at least 7 days before cutting.

items.heading: Your supplied fabric
paragraphs: You can send us your own fabric, or we can import it from your mill once you give us the supplier name and fabric code.

items.heading: Fibre and swatch checks
paragraphs: Before cutting, we check the fibre content against the print method you've chosen and inspect a swatch. Nylon needs digital pigment printing.

items.heading: Schedule and quality responsibility
paragraphs: Supplied or imported fabric adds to the lead time, and if the fabric varies, more of the quality risk sits with you.

items.heading: Launch planning service
paragraphs: With our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/), we confirm the testing, documents, sampling and production schedules for your design and materials, checked against your destination market and launch date.

blocks.heading: How Sleeves, Details and Seams Shape Your Quote
paragraphs: Long sleeves take more fabric than short or cap sleeves, so they cost more per unit, and thumb loops, zips and extra panels add sewing time. We quote from your spec sheet, fabric and quantity, so list sleeve length, neckline, trims, panels and seam type from the start. A complete specification up front saves repricing later.

blocks.heading: Washing and Drying Printed and Bonded Rash Guards
paragraphs: We write the care label for each style around how it's built and decorated, and we add specific warnings for bonded seams. Rinsing, washing gently and drying in the shade protects sublimation, screen prints and heat-transfer logos.

Heat, wringing, bleach and chlorine left in the fabric damage prints, elastane and seam adhesive faster than ordinary wear does. On programme orders, passing these instructions on to whoever does the laundry keeps the garments cared for the same way. Longer instructions need a bigger label. If comfort matters more, we print the care information straight onto the garment instead.

visuals.purpose: Sets out the care steps on our labels in the order the wearer follows them.
visuals.caption: Care steps from our rash guard labels.

items.label: Rinse in fresh water
items.detail: Rinse the rash guard in fresh water after each use.

items.label: Wash cold, inside out
items.detail: Hand wash, or machine wash cold and inside out on a gentle cycle, with no bleach.

items.label: Dry flat in shade
items.detail: Dry flat in the shade, with no tumble drying or ironing. For bonded seams: no water above 30°C, no wringing and no fabric softener.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you make thermal or lined rash guards for colder water?
items.answer: Yes. We make fleece-lined thermal rash guards in brushed polyester-spandex for swimming and surfing in cool water. Fleece-lined fabrics hold warmth, but they breathe less and dry more slowly. We build the construction you choose into a pre-production sample so you can wear-test it before approving bulk.

items.question: Which fabric options keep white or light-coloured rash guards opaque when wet and stretched?
items.answer: For opaque coverage, a soft hand and strong stretch, we use a dense 220 GSM fabric of 85% polyester and 15% spandex. You can also add a lining, a double layer or a lined front panel. You judge opacity on the pre-production sample, wet and stretched on a body, not on a flat swatch. Dense fabrics breathe less and dry more slowly, and added layers and sample rounds add cost and lead time.

items.question: What anti-ride-up options can you make for surf rash guards, such as gripper hems or board-short attachment loops?
items.answer: On any surf style, we can add a silicone grip hem, a lockdown loop that ties to your board-short drawcord, or both. They keep the shirt down while you paddle and duck-dive. You wear-test your chosen option in the pre-production sample before approving bulk.

items.question: What zipper backing or chin-guard construction can you provide to prevent rubbing on zip-front rash guards?
items.answer: We sew a soft 2 cm backing strip along the full length of the zipper and fold a fabric chin guard over the collar zip pull, so the teeth and slider stay off your skin. For extra comfort at the neck, we also offer a soft coil zip with a 3 cm zip garage at the top. You check comfort by wearing the pre-production sample.

items.question: How do you limit the white base showing through dark sublimation prints when a fitted rash guard stretches?
items.answer: We print on polyester that's pre-dyed in a matching dark shade, so when it stretches, that colour shows through instead of white. Very light artwork colours can't be printed on this dark base. We also raise ink density by about 15% in the dark areas and check the sample print stretched by 30% before bulk approval. You judge the garment wet and stretched on a body.

hero.heading: Resort Wear Manufacturer for Private Label Collections
lead: Dress your customers from poolside to dinner with one coordinated range made under your label.

cta.label: Request a quote for resort wear

blocks.heading: From Poolside to Evening: Our Full Resort Wear Range
paragraphs: We make resort wear for every part of the holiday day in your range, from poolside [cover-ups](/cover-up-manufacturer/) and beach dresses to smart-casual evening looks. Our dresses include casual sundresses, maxi and midi styles, wraps, skirt sets and evening designs.

To build complete looks, you can add kaftans, sarong sets, co-ords, shirts, printed and embroidered tops, shorts, wide-leg and palazzo trousers, other pants, lightweight woven styles and layering pieces. We make plus size collections too.

blocks.heading: Custom Resort Wear Details, Luxury Fabrics and Seam Finishes

items.heading: Luxury fabric choices
items.text: If you sell to upscale holiday retail or boutique hotels, we offer linen and silk-blend resort styles as well as embroidered designs.

items.heading: Visible seam finishes
items.text: For luxury styles, we specify French seams or bias binding on every visible seam before cutting. This gives loose and sheer garments a finished interior.

items.heading: Fray-resistant construction
items.text: Linen and viscose fray with washing and wear. We enclose the edges in French seams or 1 cm self-fabric or cotton bias binding so the seams last longer.

items.heading: Covered overlocking
items.text: We use 4-thread overlock only on seams that a lining hides.

items.heading: Construction trade-offs
items.text: French seams and binding take longer to sew and cost more than overlocking. Very thick seams and tight curves limit where we can use them, and some of those styles need a lining.

items.heading: Sheer fabric coverage
items.text: Under sheer fabrics, we add a full or half lining in cotton voile or viscose, or a separate slip.

items.heading: Waist and closure options
items.text: We build waistbands with 3 cm elastic at the back or all the way round, drawcords, concealed side zips or button-and-loop closures.

blocks.heading: Custom Resort Wear Trims, Prints and Washes

items.heading: Signature detail selection
paragraphs: Choose a small set of details for each style: a wash, a trim and a construction feature. This gives your collection its identity and keeps costs predictable.

items.heading: Trims and fastenings
paragraphs: We add crochet lace, tassel and fringe edging, smocked bodices and waists, shell or wooden buttons, rope ties and drawcords.

items.heading: Prints and washed finishes
paragraphs: You can choose block, screen or digital prints. Enzyme washes, garment washes and garment dyeing give linen and cotton a softer, lived-in hand.

items.heading: Shape and construction
paragraphs: Tiered skirts, ruffles, pin-tucks, side slits and tie-front closures are construction details you can combine with the trims and finishes you choose.

items.heading: Hand-applied decoration
paragraphs: Our [Embroidery service](/swimwear-embroidery/) decorates bikinis and cover-ups with beads, sequins, stones, rhinestones, beaded chains, sequin appliqués, embroidered patches and crochet trims. The crochet is handmade, and we sew every bead and sequin onto garments individually, never gluing or heat-pressing them.

blocks.heading: Our Own Resort Wear Factory in Guangzhou, China
paragraphs: We make resort wear and swimwear ourselves in our one factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

Our [factory and company](/about-us/) have been running since 2011. One owner runs both production and export, so we control quality, cost and delivery directly. We check every order all the way through, and if you can't visit, we run audits for you over live video. We take B2B orders only, and you agree each one directly with our team. We aren't an online shop or a third-party marketplace.

paragraphs: Bulk production starts once we have your approval and your deposit.

steps.heading: Brief and sample
steps.text: We use your brief or tech pack to develop a sample for you to review.

steps.heading: Bulk production
steps.text: After you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, production takes 35 to 40 days. Your order size and the season set the exact schedule.

steps.heading: Order dispatch
steps.text: When production is finished and your order has passed its quality checks, we ship it, and that completes the manufacturing timeline.

blocks.heading: Lightweight, Breathable Fabrics Made for Warm Weather
paragraphs: We pick breathable warm-weather fabrics, weights and linings based on whether your garment is worn on its own or over swimwear.
rows: 100% linen or 55/45 linen-viscose, in 140–190 GSM plain weave.
100% bamboo viscose twill or 95/5 bamboo viscose-spandex jersey, in 120–180 GSM.
100% organic cotton voile, poplin or gauze, in 70–140 GSM.
100% viscose challis, crepe, twill or slub, in 100–150 GSM.
30/70 silk-cotton voile or 20/80 silk-viscose satin, in 70–110 GSM.

For dresses and trousers, we use 170–190 GSM linen, 130–150 GSM viscose twill or crepe, or 120–140 GSM organic cotton poplin. We fully line the body in 70–90 GSM cotton voile or viscose, or half-line skirts and trousers down to the hip.
We use unlined 70–100 GSM cotton voile, gauze, viscose chiffon or silk-cotton voile. If you want a more opaque version, we add a lining.
Breathable fabrics show through in sunlight. Heavier fabric or a full lining gives more coverage, but the garment is less airy and costs more. Hip-length half-lining doesn't suit every silhouette.

Our [sustainability provisions](/sustainability/) cover supplier sourcing to suit your design and budget, OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

blocks.heading: Private Label Resort Wear With Your Own Prints and Branding

items.heading: Your collection route
paragraphs: You can adapt our ready resort designs with your own prints, details and branding, or develop a complete custom private label collection with us.

items.heading: Fabric-specific printing
paragraphs: We digitally print linen, organic cotton and viscose with pigment or reactive inks. We keep sublimation printing for selected polyester resort fabrics.

items.heading: Swim range coordination
paragraphs: Send us your swimwear artwork or a reference swatch. We match the print and colour on the resort fabric itself so your two ranges go together.

items.heading: Print matching costs
paragraphs: If we match large motifs across seams or coordinated pieces, each garment uses 10% to 20% more fabric and needs extra time for single-layer cutting, so your unit cost goes up. If we match only at the centre front and key seams, you keep most of the visual impact and waste less fabric.

items.heading: Engineered placement prints
paragraphs: With engineered prints, we don't have to match the full repeat on every panel, but you need artwork for each panel and size. The higher setup cost pays off only on large enough orders.

items.heading: Matching knit pieces
paragraphs: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-swimwear-printing/) digitally prints soft polyester knit to match your swimsuit fabrics. We then make it into cover-ups, dresses or short suits.

items.heading: Retail-ready brand presentation
paragraphs: Our [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels service](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/) gives you industrially compostable packaging, branded accessories and heat-pressed logos inside the garment. Connected cardboard tags and individual hand-wrapping are optional. We source labels and packaging through our trim suppliers.

items.heading: New label support
paragraphs: Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) gives you three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a catalogue of our stocked styles and a short guide to launching a swimwear brand. We also offer separate design, development and manufacturing startup packages, and new labels combine these with consulting.

blocks.heading: Patterns, Size Grading and Fit Approval Before Bulk
paragraphs: We work out your dress proportions from your measurements, a reference garment, a sketch or a full technical specification. Resort dresses and trousers come in XS to 3XL; their plus-size collections stop at 4XL, an exception to the 5XL our swimwear reaches.

We fit every style on a size M model and check it against your measurement sheet. For non-stretch wovens, we grade in fixed 5 cm steps at the bust, waist and hip, and we use a separate 6 cm rule for plus sizes. Finished body measurements stay within ±1 cm. Plus sizes get their own grading rather than a stretched version of the core grade, so the proportions still work as body shape changes. The separate plus-size body fit check adds time to sampling.
Our [in-house development team](/development/) handles pattern design, grading and fit development, so you go through fewer rounds of design back-and-forth.

visuals.purpose: Shows the grading steps used at bust, waist and hip for core and plus sizes on non-stretch woven styles.
visuals.caption: Grading steps at bust, waist and hip for non-stretch woven styles

paragraphs: We fit-approve every women's resort style before bulk production. Non-stretch fitted dresses and trousers worn over swimwear get about 6–8 cm of ease at the bust and 8–10 cm at the hip. Relaxed cover-ups get 15–20 cm.

We check this extra room on a model wearing a swimsuit. Then we shape it with darts, side slits, ties or elasticated back waists so the garment doesn't look oversized. A swimsuit adds bulk at the bust and hip, so a cover-up fitted only over bare skin or underwear ends up tight or gaping once it goes over a swimsuit. Stretch fabrics and standalone styles don't get this extra ease. We fit them closer to the body.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can you make men's resort shirts and shorts, or matching family resort pieces, to go with my women's collection?
items.answer: Yes. We make men's shirts and shorts and kids' pieces alongside your women's styles. We use the same fabric and print so your men's, women's, kids' and swim looks all match. We can also put your logo on our ready-to-brand men's collection.

items.question: Which choices in a resort style, such as fabric, embroidery, length or lining, raise or lower the unit price?
items.answer: Silk and linen blends cost more than viscose or cotton, and hand embroidery costs more than machine embroidery. Maxi lengths, full skirts and full linings use more fabric and sewing time. Midi or mini lengths, partial linings and unlined styles cost less. If you take out the lining, that changes the opacity and how we finish the seams. On natural fibres, digital printing suits small runs with many colours, and screen printing costs less per piece on larger runs with fewer colours. If you switch printing methods, your colour options change. We quote fabric, length, lining, embroidery and printing separately so you can compare them.

items.question: Can the organic cotton and viscose come with recognised certification such as GOTS, OCS or FSC for my sustainability claims?
items.answer: We buy organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and viscose from mills that use FSC-certified wood pulp, and we send you the mill certificates on request. We don't hold GOTS, OCS or FSC certification ourselves, so finished garments can't carry those labels in our name. You can ask for FSC-certified paper hang tags. Which of our own certificates applies, including OEKO-TEX Standard 100, depends on the fabric you choose.

items.question: Are any of your ready resort designs in stock for wholesale, or are they all made to order, and can I see a resort catalogue?
items.answer: We make most resort designs to order, but we keep some styles in stock for wholesale. Ask for our current Resort Wear line sheet to see what's available, and we'll send you the catalogue within 1 to 2 business days.

items.question: Which of your resort fabrics support machine-washable garments, and which require hand washing, dry cleaning or special drying and ironing instructions?
items.answer: Our organic cotton, linen and bamboo can go on a gentle 30°C machine cycle. We pre-wash linen, which keeps shrinkage within 3%. Viscose sateen needs a cold hand wash or a delicate cycle, line or flat drying and ironing on low heat. We label silk blends hand wash or dry clean only. Every care label carries the care instructions you approve.

items.question: Can you manufacture resort garments using fabric and trims that we supply, and what material limitations apply?
items.answer: Yes. We use your fabric, trims, labels and packaging, or we import fabric from your mill using its supplier name and fabric code. For resort fabrics, all we need is the composition and care data. Sublimation works only on polyester. We inspect your materials when they arrive and tell you about any shortages or defects within 3 business days, before we cut.

seo.title: Cover-Up Manufacturer for Private Label | Strandmill
seo.description: Source cover-ups under your own brand from a cover-up manufacturer. Choose fabric weight and coverage, custom prints and trims, or ready stock styles.

hero.heading: Cover-Up Manufacturer for Private Label and Stock Styles
lead: Layer kaftans, sarongs, kimonos and tunics over your swimsuits, all made to your design.

cta.label: Request a quote for cover-ups

blocks.heading: Our Cover-Up Factory in China for Kaftans, Sarongs and Kimonos
paragraphs: We make cover-ups for you to layer over your bikinis and swimsuits, from kaftans, sarongs and kimonos to tunics and beach dresses. We make them, and our swimwear, in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Your range covers maxi and mini lengths and mesh, crochet and printed pieces. Silhouettes can be fitted, oversized, draped, softly structured or asymmetrical, and the style direction can be minimalist, boho, sporty, luxury or high-fashion.

blocks.heading: OEM Cover-Up Styles, Silhouettes and Design Details

items.heading: Proven or new silhouettes
paragraphs: If you start from our fitted, wear-tested patterns, you need fewer sample rounds. You can also send us references or a brief for a new design. Our beach cover-up patterns follow resort, cruise and coastal trends.

items.heading: Closures and shaping
paragraphs: Tell us which closures and shaping you want: open fronts, ties, belts, buttons or snaps, drawstring waists and hems, and side or front slits. All of these work on plain or printed fabrics.

items.heading: Necklines and sleeves
paragraphs: Pick V, round, square, off-shoulder or halter necklines, with sleeveless, cap, kimono, bell, puff or long sleeves.

items.heading: Functional finishing details
paragraphs: We add hoods, patch or in-seam pockets, tassel ties and wooden or shell buttons to set your collection apart.

items.heading: Sample-led development
paragraphs: Our [development team](/development/) handles patterns, grading and fit to cut down the back-and-forth. You approve the sample before any bulk order, so you see the quality first.

items.heading: Factory and export ownership
paragraphs: We've operated since 2011 as a [factory-owned production and export company](/about-us/). We control sourcing, cutting, sewing, finishing and inspections at each stage. You agree your order directly with our team, not through shops or marketplaces.

items.heading: Inspection and sample delivery
paragraphs: Under our [inspection and sample arrangements](/faq/), you're welcome to have SGS or BV run independent checks before shipment. You pay for courier delivery of samples, which costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

blocks.heading: Beach Cover-Up Fabrics, GSM Weights and Coverage
paragraphs: We pick each fabric first for how well it covers when wet and where you'll wear it. Its look and colour come after that.
rows: We source chiffon, cotton voile, linen, cotton, rayon, rayon challis, bamboo blends, mesh, knit mesh, lace and crochet textiles from around the world. We also supply 100% polyester or any material you specify. For beach and poolside wear, the breathable, skin-gentle options include quick-dry fabrics.
Our cotton voile, linen and rayon fabrics run from 80 to 150 GSM. They come in 100% cotton, 100% linen, linen-cotton blends and 100% viscose, including rayon challis.
Bamboo viscose comes blended with cotton or spandex. Nylon or polyester knit mesh contains spandex and comes in similar light weights or in heavier constructions for more body.
Medium-weight linen, cotton, rayon challis and bamboo blends, tighter weaves and knit jersey give coverage without a separate slip.
Open mesh, crochet, chiffon, cotton voile and lightweight rayon become more see-through when wet. That's why we wear-test every style damp before we grade the full size run.

We line pieces fully or at the bodice/body only, using lightweight polyester georgette, cotton voile or soft knit matched to the shell. Heavier fabric, denser weaves and contrasting solid panels also add coverage.
We offer sustainable and recycled fabrics for your cover-ups.

Our [sustainability credentials](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

Our [swimwear fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) includes nylon/polyester-spandex fabrics such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. On request, we also supply chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL recycled nylon, REPREVE recycled polyester and Italian Carvico fabrics.

blocks.heading: UPF, Fabric Care, Stretch and Crochet Build

items.heading: Documented sun protection
paragraphs: For a sun-protection line, we use tested UPF 50+ fabric in closed-weave or knit long-sleeve shirts, tunics and kaftans. The AS/NZS 4399 documentation rates the fabric dry and relaxed.

items.heading: UPF claim boundaries
paragraphs: Sheer, open mesh and crochet pieces are fashion layers, so they carry no UPF claim. On mixed-panel styles, the rating covers only the areas made from tested UPF fabric.

items.heading: Shrinkage and creasing
paragraphs: We pre-shrink cotton, linen and rayon before cutting, which keeps finished shrinkage within 3%. Softening or enzyme washes reduce hard creasing, and linen-rayon or linen-cotton blends wrinkle less.

items.heading: Colour and care
paragraphs: We use dyes and prints rated grade 4 or higher for fastness to light, salt water and washing. Your care instructions say to rinse in fresh water after beach wear and dry in the shade.

items.heading: Stretch knit mesh
paragraphs: Machine-knitted nylon or polyester mesh contains 5–10% spandex and stretches about 30–50%. It springs back to shape and grows very little when wet.

items.heading: Hand-crochet growth
paragraphs: Cotton or rayon crochet has little stretch and lengthens about 5–10% when damp. We pre-wash the yarn and build that drop into the pattern, or we switch to a polyester/nylon blend yarn, which grows less.

items.heading: Secure delicate construction
paragraphs: Chiffon gets French or narrow-overlocked seams, wider allowances and clean hems to stop slippage. On mesh and crochet, we secure yarn ends, bind or tape cut edges and apply an anti-fray finish to stop snagging and unravelling.

items.heading: Crochet cost trade-offs
paragraphs: Dense crochet uses about 1.5 times the yarn of open mesh and takes longer to make. Joined squares, floral medallions and 3D shells add handwork. Open stitches, larger motifs and woven panels bring the cost down.

blocks.heading: Swimsuit Cover-Up Sizes, Lengths and Fit
paragraphs: One-size cuts work for loose kaftans and sarongs. Belted, fitted and tailored cover-ups come in graded size runs.
rows: Cover-ups are an exception to our swimwear sizes: we offer S-XL, S-L and one size. For your market, we also make plus sizes and custom sizing beyond these runs.
Our one-size kaftans and sarongs fit roughly S to XL (US 4–14) and bust measurements up to 112 cm. Plus-size cover-ups, another exception, go up to 3XL.
A standard sarong measures 110 × 170 cm. A short sarong measures 110 × 90 cm.
Mini is about 80–85 cm, midi 100–110 cm and maxi 130–140 cm. We adjust any of these to your specification.
We adjust length, fit and styling on any design, including long and long-sleeve cover-ups in plus sizes.

Our [matching beachwear service](/couples-matching-swimsuit-manufacturer/) carries your print across women's, men's and kids' lines, including beach shirts, cover-ups and sarongs. Ready-to-brand men's collections are also available.

blocks.heading: Custom Cover-Up Prints, Colours and Trims
paragraphs: First we choose the printing method that suits your fabric. Then we adapt the artwork and embellishment to match it.

items.heading: Print designs and effects
paragraphs: We develop leopard, floral and other custom prints for you using digital, screen or sublimation printing, including gradient and ombré effects.

items.heading: Soft natural-fibre prints
paragraphs: On cotton voile, linen and rayon challis, water-based screen or digital inks soak into the fabric, so it keeps its soft hand and fluid drape.

items.heading: Sublimation and block limits
paragraphs: Sublimation needs polyester and doesn't work on those natural fibres. On sheer voile, we keep heavy screen-print blocks small so the fabric doesn't stiffen.

items.heading: Decorative finishing options
paragraphs: We finish your designs with embroidery, lace insertions, metallic accents and beading, and we adapt the embellishment to each fabric.

items.heading: Sheer-fabric embroidery limits
paragraphs: On chiffon, voile and mesh, we keep light, open motifs within about 10 × 10 cm and around 5,000–8,000 stitches. For larger areas we use lace appliqués, so the fabric doesn't pucker or sag.

items.heading: Removable embroidery support
paragraphs: We stitch over a water-soluble or tear-away stabiliser and remove it afterwards, so no stiff backing shows through the sheer fabric.

items.heading: Your colour references
paragraphs: For [custom colour matching](/custom-swimwear-printing/), we work from a picture you send, our own colour chart or your Pantone references.

blocks.heading: Private Label Cover-Ups, In-Stock Styles and MOQ

items.heading: Wholesale private label
items.text: We supply wholesale beach cover-ups under your label, as either custom production or ready goods.

items.heading: Stock style selection
items.text: Our ready-to-label stock includes kaftans, sarongs, pareos, kimonos, crochet tunics and mesh beach dresses for your collection.

items.heading: Core stock colours
items.text: For a ready-goods order, you choose from white, black, beige and navy as well as seasonal prints.

items.heading: Market testing route
items.text: Stock styles in core colours let you test a market or season first. You then move your best sellers into custom development.

items.heading: Minimum order quantity
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, which works for small and growing labels.

items.heading: First trial quantities
items.text: We agree first trial runs with you case by case. What production allows sets the limit on how flexible the quantity can be.

items.heading: Launch service support
items.text: Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) gives you three finished samples, twenty swatches, a stock catalogue and a launch guide. We also offer separate design-to-manufacturing startup packages and consulting.

items.heading: Contact and response
items.text: [Contact our team](/contact-us/) by email, WhatsApp or our website form. We reply to every enquiry within one business day.

blocks.heading: Wholesale Cover-Up Orders: Samples, Lead Times, Payment and Shipping

items.heading: Quote before sampling
items.text: Send us your brief or tech pack for a [quotation](/request-a-quote/). We make the sample once you agree the price.

items.heading: Standard sample timing
items.text: A standard sample is ready for you to review and approve in 10 to 15 days.

items.heading: Sample charge
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. We don't refund it or credit it against your bulk order.

items.heading: Design charge
items.text: The design fee is USD 50 per design. It covers the pattern or print and all its colourways, and we don't refund it or credit it against your bulk order.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. The exact time depends on order size and season.

items.heading: Payment and release
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the other 50% before shipment. Your goods go through a full final inspection.

items.heading: Available shipping terms
items.text: We ship your wholesale order on FOB, CIF or DDP terms, and DDP is available worldwide.

items.heading: Door delivery price
items.text: Under DDP, you pay one all-in price for delivery to your door, and we handle freight, customs and duties through our forwarding partners.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which choices make a cover-up cost more, such as maxi length, hand crochet, beading or linen instead of polyester?
items.answer: Longer maxi and kaftan cuts cost more than simpler polyester styles. So do linings, linen and other natural fibres, and branded or recycled fabrics. If you choose a branded or recycled fabric, we list the price difference as a separate line on your quote. Crochet, beading and embroidery cost more as the handwork gets denser and covers more of the garment. Screen printing adds a setup charge for each colour. To bring the price down without lowering fabric quality, cut back the handwork, shorten the length, or use digital printing for short multicolour runs.

items.question: Can you cut and sew cover-ups from fabric we supply, including delicate woven and openwork materials?
items.answer: Yes. We cut and sew the delicate wovens, lace, crochet and other openwork fabrics you send us. For cover-ups, all we need from you is the fabric's composition and care data.

items.question: How much longer do hand-crochet or hand-beaded cover-ups take to sample and produce than plain or printed styles?
items.answer: A standard sample takes 10 to 15 days. Hand-crochet or hand-beaded samples take about 5 to 7 days more, and embroidered samples take about 2 to 3 days more. In bulk production, hand beading, sequins, rhinestones and hand crochet add 1 to 2 weeks, depending on how dense the work is. Our in-house embroidery adds about 5 to 7 days. We sew every bead and sequin on your cover-ups by hand. None are glued or heat-pressed.

items.question: Which of your cover-up materials are suitable for wearing into the water rather than only layering over swimwear on shore?
items.answer: You can wear nylon or polyester-spandex swim fabrics, quick-dry polyester mesh, knit mesh and synthetic-yarn crochet into the water, and they dry fast. If your pieces are for the pool, we can supply chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life on request. Chiffon, cotton voile, linen, rayon and bamboo blends are layers for the shore. Once they're soaked, they get heavy, cling and lose their shape.

items.question: Can your cotton, linen and rayon cover-up fabrics come with certification such as OEKO-TEX or organic certification?
items.answer: Yes. Selected cotton, linen and rayon fabrics fall under our OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification for tested fabrics and trims. We buy organic cotton from GOTS- or OCS-certified mills and can send you their certificates on request. We don't hold GOTS, OCS or FSC certification ourselves, so your finished garments can't carry those labels in our name. FSC-certified paper hang tags are available on request.

items.question: Can you put my swimsuit print on a chiffon or linen cover-up so the set matches, and how close will the colours be?
items.answer: Yes. We print your swimsuit artwork on chiffon, rayon challis or linen and adjust the colour setup for each fabric. We match both runs to your Pantone references, and you approve strike-offs placed side by side. The same file looks different on swim knit than on a light woven fabric. On sheer or natural-fibre grounds, the print reads slightly softer, which the side-by-side strike-offs show before bulk.
