seo.title: Swimwear Embroidery for Stretch Fabrics | Strandmill
seo.description: Swimwear embroidery in our own Guangzhou factory: flat, 3D puff and appliqué on stretch swim fabric, Pantone-matched threads, from 50 pieces per design.

hero.heading: Swimwear Embroidery for Stretch Swim Fabrics
lead: Your logo keeps clean edges and legible small lettering when placed in low-stretch areas.

cta.label: Talk to us about embroidery

blocks.heading: Custom Embroidered Swimwear: Flat, 3D Puff, Appliqué and Patches
paragraphs: Flat embroidery keeps your logo edges crisp and your fine text readable on swimwear. For raised detail, we use 3D puff embroidery, which sits slightly above the fabric. Appliqué gives you layered texture: we lay another fabric over the base and stitch it in place. We also make embroidered patches in the size, layout and colours you specify.

blocks.heading: Branding from Small Tags to Full Garments, Made in Our Own Factory
paragraphs: We handle your branding at any scale, from small embroidered tags to coverage across the whole garment. We make your swimwear in our own factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. We start with a small logo, and we move to larger coverage once you approve a sample on your actual swim fabric.

Our [ordering FAQ](/faq/) covers how your unit cost falls as quantities rise and how we give custom best-price quotes for 3,000+ pieces, embroidered orders included. It also covers the USD 50 sample courier delivery you pay on top of sample fees, and independent pre-shipment inspection by SGS or BV.

blocks.heading: Which Swim Fabrics Take Embroidery Well
paragraphs: Embroidery works reliably on our standard nylon and polyester spandex blends from 180 gsm up, on recycled and chlorine-resistant swim fabrics, and on lined or double-layer areas. We pick the fabric and the placement together and lean towards heavier, stable blends.

We use a stretch stabiliser so the thread moves with the fabric, and we add a soft facing on the side against your skin. Designs go in low-stretch areas such as leg hems or waistbands, because placing them in high-stretch areas causes puckering. On fabrics under 150 gsm and on mesh, ribbed or crinkle textures, we limit designs to outline or light-fill logos no wider than 5 cm. A patch or a lined panel gives you another option. We test-stitch your fabric before sampling.

blocks.heading: How We Keep Stitching Flat on Stretch Fabric
paragraphs: On stretch nylon or polyester, we prevent puckering by adapting the embroidery setup to knit fabric. We don't just copy a setup made for woven fabric. We back the fabric with a stretch stabiliser, add pull compensation and a light underlay to the stitch file, and test-stitch on your fabric before sampling.

visuals.purpose: Sets out the setup we use so stretch fabric stays flat and free of puckering when embroidered.
visuals.caption: Our anti-pucker setup for stretch swim fabric

items.label: Hoop fabric relaxed
items.detail: Hooped in its natural resting state, not stretched

items.label: Back with cut-away stabiliser
items.detail: Supports the knit while it is stitched

items.label: Fit ballpoint needle
items.detail: 75/11 ballpoint needle for stretch nylon or polyester

items.label: Lower stitch density
items.detail: About 15% lower than for woven fabric

blocks.heading: Beading, Sequins and Hand-Crochet Embellishments

items.heading: Hand-sewn decoration
paragraphs: We decorate your bikinis and cover-ups with beaded details, beaded chains, sequins and sequin appliqués. We sew on every bead and sequin one at a time and never glue or heat-press them.

items.heading: Stones and rhinestones
paragraphs: If you ask for stone or rhinestone details, we sew them on by hand. We use heavy beading and stone work only on cover-ups and pieces that get light wear.

items.heading: Handmade crochet trims
paragraphs: We do all our crochet work by hand, and then we hand-sew the finished trims onto your garments.

items.heading: Fabric sourcing
paragraphs: Our [fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) covers nylon/polyester-spandex blends, including 80% nylon 20% spandex with matching linings. On request, we also source chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL recycled nylon, REPREVE recycled polyester and Italian Carvico fabrics.

blocks.heading: Embroidery Threads, Pantone Matching and Colourfastness

items.heading: Thread and colour selection
paragraphs: We only use high-quality threads, and we adjust the stitching to suit your fabric. We match your Pantone references from our wide colour range, and before sampling we check the match on your actual fabric in daylight.

items.heading: Swim-rated colourfastness
paragraphs: Our polyester embroidery threads are rated grade 4 or above for colourfastness to chlorinated pool water, sea water and sunlight, so your logos stay bright however often the suit is worn.

items.heading: Existing thread reports
paragraphs: The threads among our tested trims are covered by our OEKO-TEX Standard 100 certification, and we'll send you the reports if you ask.

items.heading: Style-specific laboratory testing
paragraphs: If your market needs a report for the threads on the style you've ordered, we arrange testing at an accredited laboratory. We pass the lab fees on to you at cost on the balance invoice.

items.heading: Production certifications
paragraphs: Our [production certifications](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

blocks.heading: Send Your Own Design or Let Our Team Create One

items.heading: Your artwork or idea
items.text: Send us finished artwork or just a rough idea. We'll either stitch your design as it is or create the embroidery pattern for you.

items.heading: Refinement through stitch-outs
items.text: We work on the pattern with you through test stitch-outs, so you can make changes while your design is still in development.

items.heading: Broader style development
items.text: Our [OEM and ODM development](/development/) starts from your design, a picture or an idea. We do pattern design, grading and fit development in-house, which cuts down the back-and-forth.

blocks.heading: Artwork Digitising and Saved DST Stitch Files
paragraphs: Our digitising service links the artwork you send us to the embroidery we produce from it and to any repeat orders you place later. As part of your project, we set up the stitch file and keep it on file for you.

blocks.heading: Working from Your Existing Embroidery Files
paragraphs: Already have a DST or other embroidery-ready file? We'll use it once a test sew-out on your swim fabric shows it works. If the file was set up for woven or non-stretch fabric without underlay and pull compensation, or it has lettering under 5 mm high, we redigitise it. Redigitising adds a one-off setup charge per design.

blocks.heading: Embroidered Logo Techniques and Minimums
rows: You need 50 pieces per design. We embroider by machine or by hand in standard, 3D, reflective or stone techniques, and your colours come from our available thread libraries. Flat embroidery suits most swimwear placements, and 3D puff works on low-stretch areas such as waistbands and hems. We keep stone embroidery for cover-ups and accessories.

With [Custom Printing](/custom-swimwear-printing/), heat-transfer logos are the thinnest and most flexible against your skin and suit low-wear placements. Silicone patches flex and keep their shape, with a slightly raised surface. Embroidery lasts the longest but stretches the least.
With [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/), elaborate or embroidered labels and fabric-pressed logos cost extra.

blocks.heading: From Artwork Submission to Inspected Production

steps.heading: Send your requirements
steps.text: Send us your vector artwork, colour references and placement marked on the actual garment size, using our online form or email. Tell us your design, thread and embroidery type.

steps.heading: Talk it through
steps.text: Use any of our [contact options](/contact-us/) to go through your requirements with us.

steps.heading: Agree the quotation
steps.text: In our [quotation process](/request-a-quote/), sampling starts once we've agreed the price. Embroidery, screen-printing and label quotes reach you within one business day. Cut-and-sew or sublimation quotes take 2 to 3 working days.

steps.heading: Confirm colour and placement
steps.text: We confirm the thread colour match and the exact embroidery placement with you before we make any sample.

steps.heading: Approve your sample
steps.text: We prepare a physical or digital sample and make any changes you ask for before production. Fine lettering and designs in stretch zones need a physical stitch-out, because a digital approval alone isn't enough for them.

steps.heading: Inspect during production
steps.text: During production, we check every unit's thread, colour and alignment against the embroidery requirements you approved.

blocks.heading: Lead Times, Sample Fees, Payment and Shipping Terms
paragraphs: Finalise your artwork before you ask for a quotation, and build stitch-out approval into your sample calendar. Your confirmed schedule is set by the final stitch count and quantity.

items.heading: Standard sample timing
items.text: A standard sample is ready 10 to 15 days after we receive your brief or tech pack.

items.heading: Added embroidery time
items.text: Embroidery adds about 2 to 3 days to the sample for digitising and stitch-out approval, and about 5 to 7 days to bulk. Your quotation confirms the timing.

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. The design fee is USD 50 per design and covers its pattern or print and all its colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season. A full final inspection follows.

items.heading: Payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Available shipping terms
items.text: We ship on FOB, CIF or DDP terms, and worldwide DDP gets your order delivered to your door.

items.heading: DDP price coverage
items.text: With DDP, your all-in price covers freight, customs and duties, and we handle the delivery through our forwarding partners.

items.heading: Returns
items.text: Claims and returns on embroidered orders follow our [terms and conditions](/terms-and-conditions/).

blocks.heading: Full-Package Programmes and Embroidery on Your Finished Garments
paragraphs: We do durable embroidery for swimwear, beachwear and resort brands, and for swim-team and club kits. All of it is stitched in our own factory in Guangzhou.

items.heading: Full-package embroidery
paragraphs: On new styles, we embroider the cut panels before assembly so the lining hides the back of the stitching. We can do this as part of Full Package Production or work directly with your creative team.

items.heading: Detailed garment placements
paragraphs: We embroider bikini cups, strap tabs, lined areas and stable mesh. We also hand-embroider cup details in metallic lurex thread.

items.heading: Your finished garments
paragraphs: If you already have stock, ship us your finished swimsuits and we'll embroider them as a standalone job from 50 pieces per design. Add 3% spare garments per design to cover setup and normal loss.

items.heading: Arrival checks and compensation
paragraphs: We inspect your garments when they arrive and report any shortages or defects within 3 business days, before we stitch anything. If our error damages more garments than the spares cover, we pay you back at the documented purchase cost.

items.heading: Garment order minimums
paragraphs: Garment orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so small and growing labels can order with us.

items.heading: First trial runs
paragraphs: We agree first-trial quantities with you case by case. How flexible we can be depends on what production allows for your order.

items.heading: Launch service scope
paragraphs: Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) takes your custom bikinis and one-piece suits from consultation through development, sourcing, sampling, production, branding, quality control, packaging, worldwide shipping and after-sales support. You can customise both the garments and the packaging.

items.heading: Factory and direct ordering
paragraphs: Our [factory](/about-us/) has been running since 2011, and we take B2B orders directly, with no marketplace stores.

blocks.heading: A recent order

items.text: A six-store Spanish beachwear retailer moved logo embroidery on its own-label swimwear to our in-house team, with Pantone-matched threads and every unit checked before shipment. Embroidery defects at goods receipt fell from 6.0% to 0.8%, and first-sample approvals rose from 40% to 90%.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: How do you attach embroidered patches to stretch swim fabric, and can I order the patches by themselves?
items.answer: We sew patches on around the edge with a zigzag stitch or coverstitch, so the seam stretches with your suit. We don't use heat-seal glue backings because they lift in chlorine and salt water. Yes, you can order patches on their own, starting at 50 pieces per design.

items.question: What is the smallest lettering, the largest embroidery size and the most thread colours you can stitch in one design on swimwear?
items.answer: We can stitch lettering as small as 5 mm high with lines at least 1 mm thick. For 3D puff, the minimum is 10 mm high. One hooping fits a design up to 30 x 30 cm, and each design can use up to 12 thread colours.

items.question: Can you embroider on top of a printed swimsuit fabric or combine embroidery with sequins and appliqué in one design?
items.answer: Yes. We combine embroidery with sequins, appliqué, printing, laser cutting or embossing. Once your sublimation or digital print is set, we stitch over it and match the thread to your print colours. Beads and sequins go on after the embroidery, away from seams and straps, so they don't rub or snag.

items.question: What drives the embroidery cost on my order: stitch count, colours, size, technique or number of logo positions?
items.answer: Stitch count affects cost the most, and fill density drives stitch count more than size does. A solid fill costs more than an outline of the same size. Each logo position needs its own hooping and machine run. Extra colours, 3D puff, appliqué and patches add setup and handling time, and digitising adds a one-off setup charge per design. If you choose outline or open-fill designs with fewer positions and colours, you keep your cost down and the suit stays comfortable.

items.question: Can you scale the same embroidered logo across children's and adult sizes while keeping its lettering and detail readable?
items.answer: Yes. We make 2 to 3 size versions, for example about 4 cm wide for children's sizes and 7 cm wide for adult sizes. We redigitise each version instead of shrinking the file, so the lettering stays at least 5 mm high and fine detail stays readable.

items.question: Can you embroider fabric or pre-cut swimwear panels supplied by us, rather than only your own production or finished garments?
items.answer: Yes. We embroider fabric or pre-cut swimwear panels that you supply, from 50 pieces per design. 3% spare panels are added to cover setup and machine loss.

items.question: Which appliqué fabrics do you offer that remain compatible with the base fabric's stretch and wet-use requirements?
items.answer: We use a stretch swim fabric similar to your base fabric, so both layers stretch and dry together. The options are 80% nylon 20% spandex and polyester spandex, and on request chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, recycled ECONYL nylon and REPREVE polyester. We also offer metallic foil spandex, swim-grade sequin fabric and stretch mesh. We edge them with a stretch satin stitch and back them with a soft facing for wet use.

seo.title: Swimwear Consulting: Line Plans & Cost Sheets | Strandmill
seo.description: Swimwear consulting from a factory-backed team: market research, line plans and cost sheets, channel strategy and financial models, by project or retainer.

hero.heading: Swimwear Consulting for Brands, From Strategy to Production
lead: Make the business decisions behind your label with a team that sees production costs every day.

cta.label: Talk to us about consulting

blocks.heading: Swimwear Brand Consulting Built on Execution, Not Theory
paragraphs: We work with founders and executives on the business decisions that shape a swimwear brand. Our swimwear consulting covers how you position the business, what each unit earns, how and where you source, which sales channels you sell through and where you put your capital.

blocks.heading: What Our Consulting Covers and How It Differs From Design Support
paragraphs: Consulting ends with a written business strategy. Design and development support ends with patterns, fits and samples. Our consulting team handles the business decisions. Our in-house design team handles pattern design, grading, [fit development and sampling](/development/) alongside manufacturing.

Tell us whether you need a business problem solved or a product made. We scope and invoice the two services separately, so you can book either one on its own. Finish the strategy before product work commits you to fabrics and price points.

For new labels, our [Launch Services starter pack and separate startup packages](/swimwear-launch-services/) give you three finished samples, twenty fabric swatches, a stocked-style catalogue and a short launch guide. You also get separate design, development and manufacturing support for your first collection.

visuals.purpose: Shows the reader how consulting and design support differ in scope and output, so they can choose the one their problem needs.
visuals.caption: Consulting and design support are two separate services with different outputs.

rows.label: What it covers
values: Positioning, unit economics, sourcing strategy, sales channels and capital
Pattern design, grading, fit development and samples

rows.label: Who does the work
values: In-house design team, as hands-on product work

blocks.heading: Senior Consultants Backed by Our Own Factory
paragraphs: A senior consultant leads your engagement. They have at least 10 years of experience in swimwear and apparel brands, sourcing and finance, and a research and modelling analyst supports them. You work with them directly, with no agents in between.

Before any cost, fabric or lead-time assumption goes into a deliverable, we check it with our design team and production floor. Those checks use our own factory data. An assumption about another vendor needs that vendor's quote.

We make swimwear in our single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Because of our [company and factory ownership](/about-us/), production and export sit within one company, so quality, cost and delivery stay under our direct control.

blocks.heading: Market Sizing, Customer Research and Brand Positioning

items.heading: Market size and segments
paragraphs: We estimate your addressable market and split it into segments. You get customer profiles and an overview of the competitive landscape.

items.heading: Target market coverage
paragraphs: One project covers up to 3 target markets, including the US, EU, UK, Australia or Canada. We size and segment each market separately.

items.heading: Local selling windows
paragraphs: We map swim seasons, roughly March to August in the Northern Hemisphere and September to February in the Southern Hemisphere, along with year-round resort demand. That way your demand estimates and launch timing line up.

items.heading: Desk research boundaries
paragraphs: Our standard research draws on market data, competitor ranges, retail prices and customer reviews. It tells you what competitors sell and what they charge, but not why customers choose them.

items.heading: Direct customer research
paragraphs: When fit or price is uncertain, interviews or surveys test what customers prefer. On request, we add 8 to 12 interviews with target customers or an online survey of around 200 respondents.

items.heading: Positioning grounded in gaps
paragraphs: Once the market and competitor analysis is done, you get a positioning statement, brand architecture and price-value map. The positioning goes after gaps competitors leave open instead of repeating the founder's preferences.

blocks.heading: Line Plans, Target Cost Sheets and Vendor Comparisons
paragraphs: You get a line plan, target cost sheets and a sourcing strategy, all worked backward from your target landed cost and our minimums.

items.heading: Collection depth first
items.text: When something has to give, we cut styles or colourways before we touch fabric or construction quality. A narrower launch gives your customers fewer choices, but it improves sell-through and protects quality.

items.heading: Range and launch dates
items.text: We time your drops to each market's season and plan your bikini sets, separates and one-pieces. A first collection uses 8 to 12 styles in 2 to 3 colourways.

items.heading: Size range planning
items.text: We set your size range, for example XS to XL, and add cup-sized tops from B to DD where you need them.

items.heading: Minimum order quantities
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour. A matched bikini set counts as one piece, and separates count individually. We check your choices against your budget.

items.heading: Cost option comparisons
items.text: Your target cost sheets compare sublimation with screen printing, and standard with custom-branded hardware and trims. You see the difference in landed cost and unit margin before you commit.

items.heading: Vendor assessment criteria
items.text: We compare cost, minimums, lead times, quality and certifications across our factory, other manufacturers, mills and trim suppliers.

items.heading: Freedom to source elsewhere
items.text: We judge our own offer on the same criteria. Where another source suits a style better, the comparison shows it, and you're under no obligation to manufacture with us.

items.heading: First trial runs
items.text: We agree trial quantities with you case by case, within what production allows.

blocks.heading: Ethical Sourcing Standards and Claim Compliance Reviews
paragraphs: We set ethical sourcing standards and check your claims before anything is printed. Wording the evidence doesn't support gets dropped, softened or tested, because reprinting after a challenge costs more.

items.heading: Market-specific compliance
items.text: We review your claims against up to 3 target markets, such as the US, EU and UK, and build your sustainability story around documented evidence.

items.heading: Recycled-content evidence
items.text: We check sustainability and recycled-content claims against our OEKO-TEX Standard 100, GRS, RCS and bluesign certificates, plus the GRS or RCS transaction certificates linked to your order.

items.heading: Fabric certificate limits
items.text: A fabric certificate doesn't back every finished-garment claim in every market, so your wording has to match what the documents prove for the goods you ordered.

items.heading: Sun protection claims
items.text: We check UPF 50+ claims against AS/NZS 4399 documentation. That standard rates dry, relaxed fabric, not how the fabric performs wet or stretched.

items.heading: Garment labelling checks
items.text: Before your labels and hangtags are printed, we review fibre-content and care labels, plus the drawstring and small-part rules for [children's swimwear](/children-s-swimwear-manufacturer/).

items.heading: Packaging and extra tests
items.text: We check “recyclable” and “compostable” wording on your [packaging](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/). Any additional evidence you need, including wet/stretched UPF results or reports on the styles you ordered, comes from accredited labs, and you pay their fees at cost.

items.heading: Fabric sourcing options
items.text: Through our [fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) you get matching linings, blends such as 80% nylon 20% spandex and, on request, LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE and Italian Carvico.

blocks.heading: Sales Channels, Online Returns and Wholesale Timing

items.heading: Wholesale cash trade-off
paragraphs: Wholesale ties up cash in production earlier and earns a lower margin per unit than direct sales, so we let its calendar set production dates before we build your online pricing.

items.heading: Channel strategy outputs
paragraphs: We plan your mix of direct-to-consumer and wholesale sales. You get a channel strategy, a pricing and promotions framework, and an e-commerce roadmap.

items.heading: Online fit and returns
paragraphs: We build size guides, fit notes and model measurements into your product pages, allow 25 to 35% for returns in your online margins and review return reasons every season. If you leave returns out, your margin looks higher than it really is.

items.heading: Wholesale calendar first
paragraphs: Buyers place orders 6 to 9 months before the selling season. We schedule line sheets, samples and production around those windows so bulk orders arrive before stores need them. If you miss the window, you lose that season.

Our sales and marketing strategy defines your sales funnel, your target wholesale accounts and the metrics you track. You get a go-to-market plan, a marketing mix, funnel KPIs, target account lists and outreach materials for your team to put to work.
Before handover, name someone on your team to own wholesale outreach. Your team makes the contacts, so buyer relationships stay with your brand and not with an outside adviser.

When it's time to execute, Launch Services has our partner crew shoot your campaign photography and video, produces branding and e-commerce content and builds your online store. We then hand it all over for you to own and run. Wholesale sales calls aren't part of Launch Services.

visuals.caption: The strategy gives your team the plan, Launch Services can produce the content, and wholesale relationships stay with you.

values: Go-to-market plan, marketing mix, funnel KPIs, target account lists and outreach materials
Campaign photography, video, branding, e-commerce content and a built online store

Handed over for you to own and run

blocks.heading: Financial Models, Margins and Inventory Planning

items.heading: Unit economics and capital
paragraphs: We analyse what each unit earns, build gross margin bridges and assess how quickly you recover your cash. You get a financial model, a margin analysis and a capital-needs plan.

items.heading: Pre-launch model inputs
paragraphs: Before you make your first sale, we work from your target prices, landed-cost estimates based on real fabric and production quotes, and swimwear benchmarks for conversion, returns and acquisition costs.

items.heading: Three financial scenarios
paragraphs: We model conservative, base and upside scenarios that are ready for investor scrutiny. Once you start selling, you swap the benchmark assumptions for your actual results.

items.heading: Seasonal size planning
paragraphs: We size your first buy to the selling window and build its size curve from fit data and category benchmarks, for example S:M:L:XL at 1:2:2:1.

items.heading: Restocking proven sellers
paragraphs: Your first buy stays small and focuses on core sizes. Repeat orders take 35 to 40 days and restock your best sellers, so you don't tie up cash in excess stock upfront.

items.heading: End-of-season cash protection
paragraphs: We build markdowns into your cash forecast. Unsold sizes and colours are the most common reason a young swimwear brand runs short of cash before its second season.

blocks.heading: Process Improvement and Team Structure
paragraphs: Before you hire anyone, we map your processes and set out who makes which decisions. Our operations optimisation work gives you a process map, a KPI dashboard and a cost-reduction roadmap, backed by performance management.

Our organisational structure and talent work clarifies roles, assigns decision rights and sets hiring priorities together with you. You get an organisation design, a hiring plan and an analysis of what to build in-house and what to hand to partners. Clear responsibilities and a short KPI list show you where the gaps are, and your first hires fill the roles partners can't cover well.

visuals.caption: Two workstreams, each with its own deliverables.

values: Map your processes and set up performance management
Clarify roles and decision rights, and decide with you which hires come first

values: Process map, KPI dashboard and cost-reduction roadmap
Organization design, hiring plan and an in-house versus partner analysis

blocks.heading: Fixed-Scope Projects and Choosing an Engagement Format

items.heading: Fixed-scope launch projects
paragraphs: Your pre-launch decisions make up a finite project with agreed objectives, deliverables and timeline. We fix the schedule at the start: 6 to 8 weeks from initial consultation to implementation roadmap.

items.heading: Single workstream timing
paragraphs: A focused workstream, such as sourcing strategy, takes 3 to 4 weeks and settles the decision you need without you commissioning a full brand project.

items.heading: Weekly working sessions
paragraphs: Fixed-scope engagements include one 60-minute working session a week over video, and you can attend any session in person at our Guangzhou factory.

items.heading: Changes agreed before work
paragraphs: On every consulting engagement, we agree any scope change with you in writing and quote it before the extra work starts.

items.heading: Choosing your format
paragraphs: If you have a quick question, start with a one-off session. Fixed-scope work settles your launch decisions, and a retainer supports ongoing review once you have live sales and production results.

blocks.heading: Advisory Retainers: Sessions, Billing and Notice

items.heading: Scheduled advisory time
items.text: If you're scaling your brand, the advisory retainer gives you two 90-minute working sessions a month with senior advice.

items.heading: Between-session access
items.text: Between sessions, you can email or message your senior advisor. We reply within one business day to quick checks that unblock your team.

items.heading: Focused decision sessions
items.text: Bring a short list of decisions to each session. Detailed pricing, sourcing and range planning belong in focused working time, not in messages.

items.heading: Monthly retainer payment
items.text: We invoice consulting separately from production. You pay your retainer at the start of each month by T/T bank transfer in USD or EUR.

items.heading: One-off session payment
items.text: You pay for a one-off consulting session in full before it starts, also by T/T bank transfer in USD or EUR.

items.heading: Minimum term and notice
items.text: A retainer runs for at least 3 months. After that, either of us can end it with 30 days' written notice.

blocks.heading: How Engagements Start: Inputs, Steps and a Roadmap
paragraphs: Before we start, send us your target markets, delivery countries, expected quantities, budget and launch date, plus any sales, margin and cost data you have.

steps.heading: Agree the engagement
steps.text: In the initial consultation, we agree the problem, scope and outcomes with you before the work begins.

steps.heading: Diagnose the business
steps.text: We work from your real quantities, costs and margins. If you don't have sales data yet, we work from your brand brief, target prices, competitor benchmarks and our production cost estimates.

steps.heading: Design the recommendations
steps.text: We base every recommendation on costs and order sizes, so it still works once your styles reach sampling and bulk production.

steps.heading: Decide the implementation
steps.text: We tie the outcomes we agreed to implementation decisions and lay out the work in a roadmap your team can carry out.

steps.heading: Deliver the roadmap
steps.text: You get an implementation roadmap with owners, milestones and KPIs, so it's clear who is responsible for what and how progress is measured.

steps.heading: Continue into execution
steps.text: An advisory retainer reviews your progress against the roadmap. For product recommendations, we also offer design, fabric sourcing, production in our factory and delivery.

blocks.heading: Samples, Bulk Production, Payment and Shipping Terms

items.heading: Standard sample timing
items.text: Working from your brief or tech pack, we have a standard sample ready in 10 to 15 days.

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50. Design costs USD 50 per design, pattern or print, and that covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited against your bulk order.

items.heading: Bulk production timing
items.text: Once you approve the sample and we receive your deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Order size and season set the exact timing.

items.heading: Production payment schedule
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before it ships.

items.heading: Final inspection and shipment
items.text: We carry out a full final inspection, then ship your order on FOB, CIF or DDP terms.

items.heading: Worldwide DDP delivery
items.text: DDP is available worldwide. You pay one all-in price for delivery to your door, and we handle duties, customs and freight through our forwarding partners.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Can I hire you for consulting without placing a production order, including if I keep my existing manufacturer?
items.answer: Yes. Consulting doesn't require a garment order or any production commitment. You can stay with your existing manufacturer and use us for strategy only.

items.question: Is this consulting meant for a brand at my stage, from pre-launch to established label?
items.answer: Yes. We tailor the scope to your stage, whether you're a founder before launch, a label on its first collection, a direct-to-consumer brand moving into wholesale or an established label repositioning.

items.question: Can I commission only one workstream, such as sourcing strategy or financial planning, rather than a full brand consulting project?
items.answer: Yes. A single workstream has its own fixed scope, deliverables and timeline, and you can add others later. One workstream takes 3 to 4 weeks.

items.question: What decides how much a project or retainer will cost me?
items.answer: Each consulting fee is quoted to your brief. A fixed-scope project is priced on its workstreams, deliverables and weeks of work, and you pay 50% on signing and 50% on delivery. A retainer is priced on its monthly sessions and the advisory time between them, billed monthly in advance for at least 3 months. Send us your target markets, quantities, budget and launch date, and we confirm your fee in writing before any work starts.

items.question: Do we own the models and strategy documents you deliver, and can we use them with other suppliers or investors?

seo.title: Swimwear Development: Patterns, Grading & Fit | Strandmill
seo.description: Get swimwear development from patterns to approved samples: graded size ranges, colour and print mockups, and trim sourcing with costing for production.

hero.heading: Swimwear Development from Your Idea to an Approved Sample
lead: Your own sketch becomes a new style, with a fit sample for you to approve first.

cta.label: Talk to us about development

blocks.heading: Ready Design, Custom Design or a Mix?
paragraphs: For swimwear development, you can choose our ready designs, develop custom swimwear, or combine both in one collection. Our ready designs already have finished patterns and grading. If you only change colours or prints, or add your own hardware, you skip sampling and order bulk straight away. If you change the fit or construction, we make a new fit sample first. We manufacture your swimwear ourselves, in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China.

blocks.heading: Quality Checked at Every Stage of Your Order
paragraphs: Our [factory ownership and quality controls](/about-us/) keep production and export within one company. That puts quality, cost and delivery under our direct control, and we run checks throughout your order. When you [enquire about development](/contact-us/), we assign you a dedicated swimwear specialist, who arranges a call back to talk through your project.

visuals.purpose: Shows the order of the quality checks that every order goes through, from fabric arrival to final inspection.
visuals.caption: Quality checks at every stage of an order

items.label: Fabric on arrival
items.detail: Incoming fabric is checked when it reaches the factory.

items.label: Cutting
items.detail: Cut pieces are checked at the cutting stage.

items.label: Sewing
items.detail: Garments are checked during sewing.

items.label: Random checks
items.detail: Random checks are made on finished pieces.

items.label: Full final inspection
items.detail: Every order gets a full final inspection.

blocks.heading: What You Can Send Us to Start

items.heading: Your starting reference
paragraphs: Send us annotated screenshots, a tech pack, a hand-drawn or digital sketch, or an existing swimsuit or lingerie piece, and we build your custom prototype from it.

items.heading: Details beyond drawings
paragraphs: Development is anchored on your most concrete reference. If you start from a sketch, marked-up photos give us the details a drawing leaves out, including sewing, cleavage, waist and back coverage.

items.heading: Accepted file formats
paragraphs: We take CAD files in DXF (Gerber/AutoCAD) and DGS formats, and tech packs in whatever format you already use.

items.heading: Included development work
paragraphs: The per-design fee covers creating a tech pack from your sketch, along with the CAD pattern or print across all its colourways.

blocks.heading: Bust Support and Construction Options
paragraphs: We match bust support to your silhouette, your fabric and the support your customers need. We don't add every option available.

items.heading: Padding and cups
paragraphs: You can choose sewn-in or removable padding, moulded cups in sizes A to DD, and foam padding to suit your style.

items.heading: Support and construction
paragraphs: You can choose from underwire channels, removable cup pockets, power mesh, metal back-strap adjusters, invisible seams, high-cut legs and your own branded accessories.

items.heading: Fabric choices
paragraphs: Our [swimwear fabrics](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) include nylon or polyester blended with spandex, such as 80% nylon 20% spandex, with matching linings. When you request them, we also offer chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL, REPREVE or Italian Carvico fabrics.

items.heading: Materials before sampling
paragraphs: Through [Swimwear Fabrics & Sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/), you can order a USD 80 swatch pack delivered door to door by DHL Express. It isn't credited against bulk orders.

blocks.heading: Pattern Making, Size Grading and Fit Approval
paragraphs: Our in-house team takes care of pattern design, grading and fit development, so there's less back-and-forth over your design.

steps.heading: Digital pattern drafting
steps.text: We draft your patterns to your size chart in 2D AutoCAD, accurate to the millimetre. They're ready 3 to 5 days after we receive your tech pack.

steps.heading: Fabric-specific ease
steps.text: We calculate negative ease for the exact fabric you'll produce in, including how it behaves wet. Then we cut the fabric automatically so sample making stays fast.

steps.heading: Style assessment
steps.text: We review every private label sample for fit, drape, coverage, measurements and appearance. We also control strap tension, leg openings, symmetry and stretch recovery.

steps.heading: Structured style checks
steps.text: On structured styles, our sample review also covers underwires, cup shape and how the hardware is attached.

steps.heading: Documented fit approval
steps.text: We sign off one base size in production fabric against a measurement sheet, not just photos. Your feedback goes into revisions to the pattern and construction.

steps.heading: Full range confirmation
steps.text: Once the fit is approved, we grade the full range and sew and measure the remaining sizes. We confirm the grading of each size before production.

paragraphs: Before we start drawing, we talk with you about your target customer, your requirements, the styles you need, your design goals and your brand guidelines. We support both OEM and ODM development, including projects that start with an idea instead of finished technical files. Your tech pack records the measurements, materials, construction and design specifications. The technical flat drawings show seam types, where the elastic goes and the closures.

blocks.heading: What the Service Covers and Who Owns the Patterns

items.heading: Development through production
paragraphs: Our service covers pattern making, swimwear product development, size grading, marker making, sampling and bulk production. We work at a scale that keeps smaller launches affordable.

items.heading: Development without bulk
paragraphs: You can book patterns and samples on their own without committing to bulk. If you book both with us, development and production stay together.

items.heading: Your custom files
paragraphs: On fully custom projects, the tech packs and CAD patterns we develop become yours once you've paid the related fees.

items.heading: Certified production
paragraphs: Our [production credentials](/sustainability/) cover OEKO-TEX Standard 100, GRS, RCS, bluesign, ISO 9001 and WRAP.

blocks.heading: Size Ranges and Grading for Every Style
rows: We grade from XS to 3XL using internationally recognised body measurements, and we shift sizes up or down to suit your customers.
Our Plus Size Swimwear range takes grading up to 5XL.
For cup-sized women's swimwear, one-pieces, bikinis and plus-size styles, we work to your chart, including 32B–38DD. Each combination counts as one size.
The breakdown we see most often is 2-S, 4-M, 4-L, 2-XL.
Your core run serves your main customer base. Extended sizes follow once your sales establish demand.

blocks.heading: Colours, Custom Prints and Mockups

items.heading: Collection mockups
paragraphs: We make custom prints in-house. Once you've picked your colours or prints, we prepare mockups for you to approve. If you ask, we also make a free 2D mock-up of your full collection before cutting.

items.heading: Physical colour approval
paragraphs: Before production, we send you sample colour swatches. You sign off colours on physical swatches or a strike-off, not on screen mockups.

items.heading: Printed sample timing
paragraphs: Samples in the actual printed fabric take about one week longer. You can check your print on an A4 strike-off instead.

items.heading: Artwork development
paragraphs: Our [Custom Printing service](/custom-swimwear-printing/) takes your artwork as it is, adjusts it or creates it for you, then prepares the production files. New styles and bulk runs go through digital design approval and a physical sample sign-off.

blocks.heading: Hardware, Labels and Packaging Alongside Your Samples
paragraphs: With our [Swimwear Hardware service](/swimwear-hardware/), logo or custom-colour hardware samples are ready about 2 to 3 weeks after you approve the artwork. Standard colour-matched parts take 7 to 10 days. Bulk hardware starts only after you sign off, and we can fit the approved parts onto your garment sample.

Through [Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels](/swimwear-packaging-custom-brand-labels/), we develop and review your labels, hang tags, hygiene liners and packaging at the same time as your garment samples. Your branding is locked before bulk, and making those decisions early takes several weeks off your production schedule.

visuals.purpose: Shows how long a physical hardware sample takes for custom logo or custom-colour parts compared with standard colour-matched parts.
visuals.caption: Time to a physical hardware sample

blocks.heading: Component Sourcing and Production Preparation

items.heading: Full or partial sourcing
items.text: We source fabrics, elastic, hardware and tags for you from trusted suppliers. Choosing components takes around 1 week, and longer with some suppliers.

items.heading: Choices before costing
items.text: We settle your components before the samples are finished. That way the consumption report and bulk costing match the materials that go into production.

items.heading: Bulk component orders
items.text: Before mass production, we report how much of each component your order uses and work out the production cost. Then we help you order the components you need.

items.heading: Your supplied materials
items.text: You can send us your own fabric, trims, hardware and labels for sampling. We can also import from your mill if you give us the supplier name and fabric code.

items.heading: Sampling fabric quantities
items.text: For sampling, send about 1.5 metres of each fabric and lining for each style in each colour.

items.heading: Bulk fabric allowance
items.text: For bulk, send 5% extra fabric. It has to reach our factory at least 7 days before cutting is scheduled.

blocks.heading: What Samples Cost and How Approval Works

items.heading: Standard sample timing
items.text: Your standard sample is ready for review in 10 to 15 days.

items.heading: Sample and design fees
items.text: Each sample costs USD 50, and the design fee is USD 50 per design. We don't refund either fee or credit it against your bulk order.

items.heading: Sample delivery charge
items.text: [Sample courier delivery](/faq/) costs USD 50 on top of the sample fee.

items.heading: Prototype feedback
items.text: We send you fitting or prototype samples before pre-production approval. You give us feedback, ask for changes and make final adjustments.

items.heading: Binding bulk reference
items.text: We schedule bulk only after you approve the pre-production (PP) sample. That sample is the binding reference, and we check production against it.

items.heading: Completed order details
items.text: When your goods are ready, we send you a packing list with the quantities and sizes for each style.

items.heading: Embroidery timing
items.text: [Embroidery](/swimwear-embroidery/) adds about 2 to 3 days to sampling and 5 to 7 days to bulk. Your quotation confirms the exact timing.

items.heading: Returns
items.text: Claims and returns on development and sample orders follow our [terms and conditions](/terms-and-conditions/).

blocks.heading: Fit Sampling, Wet Testing and Approval

steps.heading: Plain first sample
steps.text: For a custom design, we get the fit right on a white or black sample first. Then we move on to the colours or prints you've chosen.

steps.heading: Live model fitting
steps.text: A real person wears every fit sample. The base size is M for standard styles and 2XL for plus-size swimwear.

steps.heading: Dry and wet testing
steps.text: We try the same suit on the fit model dry, then in water, and compare how it stretches, covers and stays opaque.

steps.heading: Correcting wet opacity
steps.text: If the fabric goes see-through when wet, we add or replace the lining or switch to a heavier fabric. Then we wet-test it again before we send you your approval sample.

steps.heading: Revising failed fit
steps.text: If you don't approve the fit, we amend the patterns and make new samples after each fitting. Most samples are approved in the first round.

steps.heading: No-charge corrections
steps.text: Minor digital adjustments take minutes and are free. If a sample differs significantly from the approved handover, we remake it at no extra cost.

blocks.heading: Starting With Samples Before Bulk
paragraphs: Most of our partnerships start with samples, so you can judge our quality for yourself before you place a bulk order. Once you approve a sample and pay the deposit, bulk production takes 35 to 40 days, depending on order size and season.

blocks.heading: Minimums, Payment and Shipping Terms

items.heading: Order minimum
items.text: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so ordering stays accessible for small and growing labels.

items.heading: First trial run
items.text: We agree your first trial quantities case by case. How flexible we can be is limited by what production allows.

items.heading: Payment split
items.text: You pay a 50% deposit when you confirm the order and the remaining 50% before shipment.

items.heading: Shipping terms
items.text: We ship FOB, CIF or DDP. Worldwide DDP gives you one all-in price delivered to your door, and we handle the duties, customs and freight through our forwarding partners.

blocks.heading: Bulk Lead Times and Extra Time for New Moulds or Prints

steps.heading: Finalise custom development
steps.text: You finalise any new mould or custom print before you book bulk, so development time stays separate from production time.

steps.heading: Allow additional time
steps.text: Any style that needs a new mould or print needs an extra 2 to 3 weeks.

steps.heading: Meet production prerequisites
steps.text: The bulk production lead time starts from your approved sample and our receipt of your deposit.

steps.heading: Plan bulk production
steps.text: Bulk production takes 35 to 40 days. Your order size and the season decide where your schedule falls in that range.

blocks.heading: Related products and services
Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: If I send another brand's swimsuit, will you copy it exactly, or do you only use it as a reference for fit and construction?
items.answer: We use your reference swimsuit for fit, construction and sizing. We don't copy another brand's logos, trademarked prints or protected design details. We measure the reference and turn it into a spec sheet with tolerances, then build the pattern and make the changes you've asked for. Your finished style carries your own branding and artwork.

items.question: If I launch with ready-to-go styles, could other brands sell the same designs, and how does that compare with the custom route?
items.answer: Yes. Our ready-to-go designs are non-exclusive and stay available to every buyer, so other brands can sell the same base styles. Your prints, artwork and branding are used only for you, though. Any custom or ODM design we develop for your brand is exclusive to you, and we'll sign an NDA if you ask.

items.question: What measurement tolerances do you work to when you check samples and graded sizes against my spec sheet?
items.answer: We check every sample and every graded size against your spec sheet. Straps, bindings and any measurement under 10 cm can be off by no more than 0.5 cm either way (-0.5 to 0.5 cm). Body measurements can be off by no more than 1 cm either way (-1 to 1 cm).

items.question: Can you show my styles as 3D virtual samples before you sew a physical prototype, or do you only offer 2D mockups?
items.answer: Yes. Before we sew your first physical prototype, we make 3D virtual samples free of charge, on top of our free 2D collection mockups. You check the proportions, where your artwork's print sits and the colours on screen, so you need fewer rounds of physical samples.

hero.heading: Swimwear Packaging & Custom Brand Labels
lead: Put your brand on every tag, label and bag so each piece looks like yours when unboxed.

cta.label: Talk to us about swimwear packaging & custom brand labels

blocks.heading: Branded and Ready to Sell, or Packed in Your Own Materials
paragraphs: We finish your swimwear order with hang tags, garment labels, hygiene liners and bags, so every piece leaves our factory branded and ready to sell. If you'd rather supply your own labels or packaging, we attach them and pack your finished pieces in your own materials.

blocks.heading: Branding Add-On Costs and Supplying Your Own Materials
paragraphs: Each branding extra, from embroidered labels and DTF logos to printed bags and branded liners, adds to your per-piece cost, and we list each one separately on our quotation. Start with one or two customer-facing extras to keep your first selection focused, then let sales guide what you add on reorders. We check any materials you supply and report issues before cutting.

visuals.purpose: Shows the steps and deadlines for buyers who send us their own labels, hang tags and bags.

items.label: Count and check

items.label: Report any issues

blocks.heading: Packed and Labelled in Our Own Guangzhou Factory
paragraphs: We make and pack your swimwear in our own single factory in Guangzhou, Guangdong, China. Our [Launch service](/swimwear-launch-services/) takes your custom bikinis and one-pieces from your brief through fully customisable development, production and worldwide delivery, and on to after-sales support. We've run our [factory-owned production and export operation](/about-us/) since 2011. That keeps quality, cost and delivery under our direct control, and we check your order from incoming fabric through to final inspection. Our [sustainability work](/sustainability/) covers OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics and trims, GRS and RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance. It also covers corn-starch bags for industrial composting and reusable eco zip-lock bags.

blocks.heading: Custom Swimwear Labels, Branded Bags and Lead Times
paragraphs: We develop and approve your swimwear labels and packaging alongside your samples. When your branding is settled before bulk production, your schedule is several weeks shorter.

items.heading: Main label choices
paragraphs: We build your branding into production with woven main and neck labels, plus satin, cotton, transparent, stamped, printed, heat-transfer and silicone options.

items.heading: Care and size labels
paragraphs: Your care, wash and size labels come woven, printed or heat-transferred. Heat-transfer care labels keep the suit tagless, and woven or printed labels come with recycled-material options.

items.heading: Finished garment logos
paragraphs: If you want branding on the finished piece, we print your logo after sewing. Labelling is an add-on and doesn't count towards your garment minimum quantities.

items.heading: Sampling and mockups

paragraphs: Choose your bag by how your customers will dispose of it. Corn-starch garment bags go to industrial composting. Eco zip-lock bags are made to be reused.
rows: A blend of about 60% corn starch and 40% PBAT, a polymer that breaks down under industrial composting.
We chose these after trialling other compostable options. They protect your pieces from humidity in storage and on sale.

paragraphs: We match DTF logos to your Pantone references and place them on the outside of the suit.

items.heading: Flat fabrics only
paragraphs: Our testing supports DTF on all flat swimwear and activewear fabrics. Textured fabrics need a different branding option.

items.heading: Dimensions and sampling
paragraphs: We produce DTF at any size up to 35 x 10.7 cm (13.8 x 4.2 in), and a DTF sample takes 2-3 days.

items.heading: Solid logo limits
paragraphs: DTF stretches far less than swim fabric, so large solid logos stiffen the area and lift or crack when stretched. For that reason, solid areas on stretch zones are capped at 8 x 8 cm.

items.heading: Placement and open designs
paragraphs: We turn larger artwork into outlines or open designs with gaps of at least 1 mm. We place logos on lower-stretch areas: hips, centre backs or leg hems.

items.heading: Thickness and durability
paragraphs: DTF is about 0.2 to 0.3 mm thick, so it's firmer, less stretchy and longer-lasting. Inside heat transfers are about 0.1 mm thick and softer, and they move with the fabric.

blocks.heading: Embroidered Logos for Stretch Swim Fabrics
paragraphs: Our [Embroidery service](/swimwear-embroidery/) adds embroidered logos at low-stretch hems or waistbands on swim fabrics from 180 gsm; on lighter or textured fabrics, we use small outline logos or patches.

blocks.heading: Hang Tag Shapes, Paper Stocks and Finishes
paragraphs: We match the shape and board weight of your hang tag to your brand's look and to the size of the garment.

items.heading: Six shape options
items.text: You can choose from 6 hang-tag shapes: rectangles, squares, a circle and an oval. Each one is sized for a different way of presenting the garment.

items.heading: Rectangle dimensions
items.text: For a rectangular branded hang tag, choose 5 x 9 cm, or 4 x 10 cm for a slim version.

items.heading: Square dimensions
items.text: Our standard square and our rounded-corner square are both 6 x 6 cm, so you get two corner styles at the same size.

items.heading: Circle and oval
items.text: The round hang tag is 6 cm across. For a narrower format, the oval is 5 x 8 cm.

items.heading: Paper and finishes
items.text: You can have 350gsm, 400gsm or 600gsm paper board, or 350gsm or 400gsm recycled stock. Each comes in black or white, with a gloss or matte finish.

items.heading: Printed brand details
items.text: Our packaging suppliers print your logo and brand details on the tag, leaving room for your brand story and QR codes.

items.heading: Branded hardware alternative
items.text: With [Swimwear Hardware](/swimwear-hardware/), each logo mould costs USD 200 and unit prices depend on the design. Resin O-rings start at 100 pieces per colour, and branded metal tags or embossed labels start at 100 pieces.

blocks.heading: Kraft Paper, Plastic and Recycled-Content Hygiene Liners
paragraphs: We choose your hygiene liners, made by our trim suppliers, based on how long they'll be stored and how humid it is. During sampling, we peel-test the liner you pick on your own lining.
rows: Comes in 5 shapes. Custom branding needs an order of more than 3,000 units, and you get a free digital mockup.
Comes in 5 shapes. Custom branding needs an order of more than 3,000 units, and you get a free digital mockup.
Made from 90% recycled materials and available in 3 shapes: thong, standard bikini and full coverage. The water-resistant adhesive peels off without residue. Custom branding isn't available.

Thong: 12 x 3.5 cm, tapered, for thong and Brazilian cuts. Kids: 9 x 4 cm. Standard bikini: 14 x 5 cm. Full coverage: 16 x 6.5 cm, for high-waist and one-piece styles. Wide: 15 x 7.5 cm, for boy shorts and fuller bottoms.

Plastic film doesn't absorb moisture, so it holds more firmly and peels off cleanly in one piece. Kraft holds fine in a normal warehouse, but above about 70% humidity it softens and curls, and after 6 months it tears when removed. If your stock will sit in humid storage for a long time, you need plastic.

The low-tack, pressure-sensitive adhesive holds on our nylon-spandex, polyester-spandex and recycled-nylon linings. It doesn't suit cotton, open mesh or brushed linings. Mesh, crochet, velvet, sequinned or coated surfaces need a sewn-in gusset instead.
In normal storage, liners stay put for up to 12 months and come off without marks or damage. Longer storage, or temperatures above 40°C, leaves adhesive behind.
Our peel test checks that the liner stays flat through 8 hours of wear and comes off in one piece with no residue, pilling or colour lift.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: Which packaging is recyclable or industrially compostable, and do those claims cover printed packs?
items.answer: Our corn-starch bags break down under industrial composting conditions, but not in home compost or landfill. Our eco zip-lock bags are reusable, and for any recycling claim we send you the material supplier's data. The supplier data covers only the bag material, not your printed finished pack. You check the disposal and warning wording against your market's and your retailer's rules, and only wording you've approved in writing goes to print.

items.question: What shelf life and storage conditions should we plan for before corn-starch bags become brittle, sticky or otherwise unsuitable for sale?
items.answer: Our corn-starch bags stay strong, clear and ready to sell for 12 months from production when they're sealed in cartons below 30°C and out of direct sunlight. Plan to sell through within that window. Long exposure to temperatures above 40°C or to direct sun shortens their life and turns the film brittle or tacky. That's why your bags are made close to shipment.

items.question: Can your bags be printed with suffocation warnings and meet FBA or retailer polybag rules?
items.answer: Yes. Our bag suppliers print suffocation warnings in the languages you choose, in type of at least 10pt. For Amazon FBA, we use 50 µm (about 2 mil) film that's clear enough for barcode scanning, and we put warnings on every bag with an opening of 12.7 cm (5 in) or wider. For other retailers, we match the thickness, warning text and label placement to the packaging manual you send us.

items.question: How do you prevent dark or sublimated swimwear fabrics from discolouring a white heat-transfer label?
items.answer: On dark, bright or sublimated fabrics, our label supplier prints white labels over an anti-migration blocker, and we press them at about 130°C so the dye doesn't bleed into the print. Before bulk, we check a pressed strike-off on each fabric. If the dye still shows through, we switch that label to black.

items.question: My collection uses textured fabric. Which label should I choose instead of a heat transfer or DTF label?
items.answer: On textured, ribbed or crinkle swim fabrics, we use an embroidered label on a low-stretch waistband or leg hem. The other option is a heat transfer on the smooth inner lining instead of the textured outside. Men's and boys' swim trunks can also take a sewn-on rubber patch.

items.question: How are hang tags attached without snagging or putting holes in the swimsuit?
items.answer: We loop cotton or recycled-polyester string, or ribbon, around a strap or through the care label, so the swim fabric is never pierced. If you'd rather have a plastic fastener or safety pin, we attach it only through the sewn-in care label or the seam allowance, never through the body fabric. We use a fine 1 mm needle so it doesn't snag.

blocks.heading: Printable Swim Fabrics, Including Recycled Options
paragraphs: We begin with the colour result and handfeel you need, then match the printing method to the fibre.

items.heading: Polyester print bases
paragraphs: We print full-colour sublimation on durable 100% polyester, performance blends and poly-blends.

items.heading: Recycled sublimation microfibre
paragraphs: We print with eco-friendly ink on a 150 g/m² microfibre made of 86% recycled polyester and 14% elastane. Recycled microfibre is also available for shorts.

items.heading: Other recycled options
paragraphs: You can choose recycled polyamide/elastane swim fabric, performance fabric for swim fit or super-soft recycled nylon. Nylon is printed with digital pigment printing.

items.heading: Your supplied fabric
paragraphs: We accept nylon or polyester blends with spandex. Sublimation requires polyester, and nylon requires digital pigment printing.

items.heading: Base fabric requirements
paragraphs: The base you send must be white or light, with no water-repellent, silicone or other coated finish.

items.heading: Testing before cutting
paragraphs: Before we cut your supplied fabric, we test it for shrinkage, colour fastness and stretch.

items.heading: Fabric sourcing
paragraphs: Our [fabric sourcing](/swimwear-fabrics-sourcing/) covers nylon/spandex and polyester/spandex with matching linings, including 80% nylon 20% spandex. It also covers chlorine-resistant LYCRA Xtra Life, ECONYL recycled nylon, REPREVE recycled polyester and Italian Carvico on request.

blocks.heading: Certified Inks That Resist Chlorine, Salt and Fading
paragraphs: If your swimwear will be used often in the pool or the sea, we sublimate onto polyester-rich fabric so the print lasts.

items.heading: Certified printing inks
items.text: Every print uses ecological inks that carry their maker's OEKO-TEX® ECO PASSPORT certification, along with OEKO-TEX® certified dyes.

items.heading: Water-based dyes
items.text: Our dyes are water-based. They bond into the fibres instead of leaving a thick layer on the surface.

items.heading: Lasting print quality
items.text: Our high-resolution sublimation prints resist chlorine, salt water and repeated washing without cracking or peeling.

items.heading: Production certifications
items.text: Our [sustainability certifications](/sustainability/) are OEKO-TEX Standard 100 for tested fabrics/trims, GRS/RCS for recycled fabrics, bluesign for chemistry, ISO 9001 for quality management and WRAP for social compliance.

blocks.heading: Artwork Files, Repeats and Design Support
paragraphs: Send your artwork at 300 dpi or higher, as vector files such as AI or PDF or as image files such as PNG or TIFF. We accept other formats too. Your artwork needs a seamless repeat or a layout that's ready to repeat. A motif repeat is typically 15–20 cm, but your design doesn't have to match that size. If you have a non-repeating image that works for it, we help you set it up as a four-way mirror.

We check the repeat seams and scale at actual garment size. If there's a tiling problem, our design team fixes it instead of sending the file back to you. You can send print-ready artwork or develop it with us, and our file-setup guidance is free.

items.heading: Placement instead of repeat

items.heading: Artwork layout options
items.text: You can choose front and back prints, sleeve branding, full-wrap graphics and gradient fades.

items.heading: Consistency across sizes
items.text: We engineer the placement on each size's cut pattern pieces, so your motifs sit in the same visual position across your whole size range.

blocks.heading: Pantone Colour Matching for Your Prints
paragraphs: We match your colours to a picture you send, to our colour chart or to Pantone references. For sublimation calibration, we prefer a physical Pantone TCX reference over TPG. You confirm the colour on a sample of the actual production fabric in daylight, so you aren't judging the result on a screen.

blocks.heading: Mock-ups, Strike-offs and Sample Approval

steps.heading: Scale and trial print
steps.text: We send you digital mock-ups so you can approve the scale, and we turn strike-offs around in one day. We then send a 30x30cm trial-print swatch so you can approve colour and quality, and we revise it as needed.

steps.heading: A4 approval options
steps.text: The fastest option is an A4 strike-off that we photograph or film and email to you, at USD 35 per motif. If you want the same A4 posted to you, it costs USD 35 plus courier.

steps.heading: Printed fabric checks
steps.text: If you need to check drape or stretch, two metres cost USD 35 per metre (USD 70) plus courier. This adds a few extra weeks.

steps.heading: Sample and design fees
steps.text: Standard samples take 10 to 15 days and cost USD 50 each. Design costs USD 50 per design, and that covers all colourways. Neither fee is refunded or credited towards your bulk order.

steps.heading: Sampling and reorder terms
steps.text: Under our [sampling terms](/faq/), you pay the courier, which costs USD 50. New moulds or prints add 2 to 3 weeks. Approved reorders skip sampling, and you're welcome to arrange independent SGS or BV inspections.

steps.heading: Development service timing
steps.text: With [Development](/development/), confirming fabric and trims takes 1 to 3 days, cards and swatches reach you within 10 days, and fit approval takes 3 to 7 days. Digital samples add about one week, and revisions add time.

items.heading: Higher-cost print treatments
items.text: Exclusive development, a placement setup for each size, and specialty metallic or fluorescent inks all cost more. Keep these treatments for your hero styles to control costs.

items.heading: Premium fabric costs
items.text: Branded and recycled print fabrics cost more than our standard print fabric choices.

items.heading: Print theme choices
paragraphs: We source nearly any colour or print for your digital-printed range, including floral, paisley, retro, zigzag, animal, strawberry, lemon and watercolour themes.

items.heading: Exclusive print development
paragraphs: We develop exclusive prints just for you, and this adds lead time. The per-design fee covers developing the print in all colourways, plus its tech pack and CAD pattern.

items.heading: Colourways for later seasons
paragraphs: If you develop one exclusive print and add colourways later, you don't pay a new design fee. Physical strike-offs and printed approval fabric are still charged separately for each motif.

blocks.heading: Minimum Order Quantities and Trial Runs
paragraphs: Orders start at 50 pieces per style in each colour, so small and growing labels have a quantity they can start with. We agree your first trial run case by case, and we can flex on quantity only as far as production allows.

Frequently Asked Questions

items.question: For your digital printing, do the number of artwork colours or the amount of printed coverage change the production cost?
items.answer: The number of colours doesn't change your digital printing cost, because every design prints in one pass at the same rate. Coverage does matter when you compare print types. We cost all-over prints by the metre of fabric, and a small placement print on a plain piece costs less than printing the whole garment.

items.question: Can you print on a black or coloured base fabric, or does my print have to go on white fabric?
items.answer: We print on black or coloured bases, but sublimation only produces tones darker than the base. All-over sublimation needs a polyester-rich fabric. Its dyes are transparent, so they give the truest colours on white or light bases and can't print lighter than the fabric. For white or pastel details, we use a white base, or digital pigment printing with a white underlayer on dark fabric.

items.question: Can I order custom-printed swimwear fabric from you without ordering garment manufacturing?
items.answer: No. We only offer custom printing on swimwear we manufacture for you, and we don't take fabric-only orders. Any printed fabric we produce ships with your garment order.
